WHY HARVEY
At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.
Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.
At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.
ROLE OVERVIEW
As an Enterprise Customer Success Manager for Law Firms at Harvey, you are the custodian of value for a portfolio of leading UK, European and international law firms — you own their mutual success plan and, with your Account Executive, their renewal. You will guide firms from first adoption to Harvey being embedded in how their practice groups work, moving each firm along the AI maturity curve by connecting our technology and legal expertise to its own goals, so partners and associates see undeniable value and the firm builds a lasting AI advantage. You will act as a trusted adviser to innovation leaders and partners, run your book as a portfolio, and orchestrate Harvey's Legal Engineers, Product and Sales teams around each firm.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
 - Deliver the firm's journey: build and run a mutual success plan tied to each firm's objectives, priorities and metrics — practice-group adoption, capacity, client propositions — and deliver kickoffs, implementation reviews, QBRs and executive business reviews to a consistently high standard.
 - Drive adoption across practice groups: move Harvey from pilot to daily use, practice group by practice group, building on proven use cases, working with Legal Engineers on tailored enablement and with partners to sponsor change; go beyond the innovation team to practice group leaders, senior and managing partners, and cultivate champions who enable others.
 - Orchestrate cross-functionally: sequence Legal Engineers, Product, Innovation Partners and the Transformation Office intentionally, and bring the voice of the firm back to Product and Engineering.
 - Prove value and expand: align each firm on measurable outcomes — capacity, realisation, matter economics, client impact — capture value stories and ROI evidence, and qualify and progress expansion with your Account Executive.
 - Run your book and own renewal readiness: know whether each firm is in Defend, Maintain or Grow with evidence; prioritise by value, renewal timing and risk; surface risk early and partner with your Account Executive to renew and expand our strategic partnerships.
WHAT YOU HAVE
Ideal candidates for the Enterprise Law Firm CSM role at Harvey can demonstrate comfort and experience with the following:
 - 5+ years in customer-owning roles — Customer Success, account management, legal-tech consulting or an innovation / commercial role inside a law firm — with law-firm customers or stakeholders.
 - An understanding of how law firms work: how partnerships make decisions, how practice groups differ, and what partners, associates and innovation teams each care about.
 - An AI-native way of working: you use AI and sophisticated tooling daily, can show how it has changed your own output, and have a point of view on how AI changes legal practice.
 - A track record of taking enterprise customers from initial adoption to embedded, organisation-wide use, with measurable outcomes grounded in concrete use cases.
 - Building multi-threaded relationships at senior level and influencing stakeholders who did not buy the product.
 - Strategic planning and revenue-based prioritisation across a portfolio, including early identification and mitigation of risk.
 - Quantifying and communicating business value and ROI to senior legal stakeholders.
 - Working cross-functionally with Sales, Legal Engineering and Product teams; comfort running in-person meetings with executives.
 - Adapting seamlessly in the face of high-speed change and growth, with a strong point of view and proactive self-management.

as-vanta-94ffa2d9-5d03-4b5d-8952-d421e08.description:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 
As Vanta continues its push into new markets, the EMEA Revenue Org is at the center of that growth — and this role is the dedicated enablement partner making that motion faster, sharper, and more scalable. As a Sr. Revenue Enablement Manager supporting our EMEA organization, you'll operate as a true strategic thought partner to Sales and Post-sales leadership, helping design and build the enablement infrastructure needed to win in complex sales environments. This is a high-autonomy role that shapes how Vanta's revenue teams learn, grow, and perform.
This role will lead the execution of both global enablement initiatives and region-specific programs. You’ll work independently, build credibility with senior stakeholders, and help EMEA leaders reinforce new skills and behaviors with their teams.
What you’ll do as a Senior Revenue Enablement Manager at Vanta:
 - Partner closely with EMEA Revenue Leadership to understand business priorities, team performance, and enablement needs.
 - Build trusted relationships with sales leadership and cross-functional partners across Revenue and the broader business.
 - Diagnose gaps in industry, product, sales methodology, and role-specific skills across EMEA.
 - Design and prioritize a regional enablement roadmap that connects global initiatives to the needs of EMEA teams.
 - Support regional onboarding where needed.
 - Create and deliver enablement programs, content, workshops, and other learning experiences that improve sales execution.
 - Partner with EMEA leaders to reinforce enablement in the field and hold teams accountable for applying new knowledge and skills.
 - Measure program effectiveness, gather feedback, and refine enablement priorities as the business, product, and sales motion evolve.
 - Collaborate with other Revenue Enablement partners to maintain alignment across global programs and regional delivery.
How to be successful in this role:
 - 5+ years of experience in sales enablement, GTM enablement, or an equivalent role.
 - Experience supporting EMEA-specific sales teams and markets.
 - Experience supporting global sales organizations in a variety of roles spanning Early Stage through Upmarket segments.
 - A track record of designing and delivering sales methodology enablement.
 - Experience in SaaS; experience supporting a technical product is preferred.
 - Strong ability to diagnose capability gaps and translate them into focused enablement priorities.
 - Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills across varied audiences.
 - Strong business partnership and cross-functional collaboration skills.
 - Ability to operate independently, manage ambiguity, and build credibility with senior sales leaders.
 - Uses AI in day-to-day work to amplify their skills and strengthen their outcomes, applying it across routine workflows, actively building fluency through experimentation, and exercising sound judgment to ensure AI-assisted work meets a high quality bar.
 - Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.
What you can expect as a Vanta’n:
 - Industry-competitive salary and equity
 - 100% covered medical, dental, and vision benefits with dependents coverage
 - 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents
 - Health & wellness stipend
 - Remote workspace, internet, and mobile phone stipend
 - Commuter benefits for team members who attend the office
 - Pension matching
 - 25 days of Annual Leave per year and unlimited sick time
 - 8 company-paid holidays
 - Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!
 - Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney
#LI-hybrid
At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.
About Vanta
We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. 
Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.

We're training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

 The role 
You'll lead marketing operations and analytics at Cohere. That covers the team, the martech stack, how we measure marketing's contribution to pipeline, and the budget and pipeline numbers marketing plans against. When leadership asks what marketing produced last quarter and what to fund next, the answer starts with your numbers.

The attribution methodology is yours, documented and signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance. A/B testing on nurture and forms sits with you too, sized so the results can be read.
Over time we want fewer tools and fewer dashboards, with one governed source for each metric.
 Budget and planning numbers 
You'll own the martech and operations budget and track budget and headcount across marketing. You'll also build the pipeline and capacity models marketing plans against. The Marketing Chief of Staff runs planning and the business reviews and leads the trade-off conversations with your numbers in hand. Marketing and Sales need to count pipeline the same way, every time.
 Your first year

"GTM Architect" or "GTM Engineer" titles are emerging as some of the fastest-growing roles in B2B SaaS, and early movers building this skillset are well-positioned.
 Compensation context: The base range of CAD $110k–$140k (OTE up to $155k) is competitive for a senior IC role at a Canadian tech company, though it trails comparable US-based roles by 20–30%. The LTIP is a meaningful differentiator for a ~20-year-old profitable company.
Agentic AI workflow design using LLMs, MCP connectors, and tools like n8n — highly transferable and in short supply.
Signal-based GTM strategy (product-led growth meets AI-driven outbound) — a rapidly maturing discipline.
SQL-backed revenue analytics tied directly to business outcomes (renewals, NRR, LTV).
Cross-functional stakeholder management without a PM — high autonomy, high visibility.
 Green flags: No bureaucratic PM layer, clear ownership of business metrics, and a company with 15,000+ paying customers providing real production data to work with. The take-home case study hiring process signals they want proven builders, not credential collectors.

Company Description
Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart — we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent , our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate , the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.
Your Role
ShareGate's customers generate rich signals (product usage, support interactions, renewal dates), but those signals aren't yet connected into an engine that protects and grows the revenue we already have. As our GTM Architect, Expansion & Retention, you'll design, build and ship AI agents and agentic workflows that turn those signals into saved renewals and cross-sell pipeline. This is an embedded engineering role within GTM, not back-office ops: you'll apply the signal-based, agent-first approach we already use for new customer acquisition to the customers we already have.

Protect renewals by building AI agents that continuously monitor renewal health and flag at‑risk accounts to Account Managers early, with context, recommended next steps and enough lead time to act.
Grow revenue from existing customers by designing and running an agentic cross‑sell motion: score fit for our second product line, research each account, personalize outreach, qualify interest and route genuine intent to the right salesperson with the full context needed to close.
Define the signals your agents need and partner with Revenue Systems, which builds and owns the data flow between product usage and the CRM. Validate the data with SQL before you act on it.

az-ca-5961481766.description:
The Opportunity: 
We are looking for a delivery-focused Project Manager to run acquisition migrations end-to-end as Beacon standardizes each newly acquired company onto a common GTM stack. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who runs several projects at once against a hard deadline, keeps a lot of moving parts coordinated, and raises the bar on the quality of work around them.
Beacon acquires roughly one software company per week which is then integrated into our standardized GTM stack. This role partners with newly acquired companies starting from the first discovery call, through CRM and Support Ticketing builds, until systems are fully rolled out. This role coordinates internal resources and ensures the portfolio company is trained on the tech stack while adhering to an SLA and making the process more repeatable with every acquisition.
This role is responsible for running the project, meaning holding the timeline, managing the stakeholders, directing the build resources, and making sure what ships is right. This role will be partnered with a technical RevOps resource to help with deeper technical support, but this role will be responsible for speaking to the toolset at a high-level.
 What You Would Own: 
 Migration delivery. Acquisition migrations against our SLA, owned end to end: scoping, project planning, sequencing the CRM and Support Ticketing builds, coordinating data migration, and making sure the team is trained and confident at go-live. You would lead discovery calls to assess their current stack and map it to Beacon's standards, hold the plan and the timeline across several concurrent migrations, manage dependencies and risks before they become slips, and own the status.
 Contractor direction and quality. You would direct the work of pooled implementation contractors assigned to your migrations, pull in technical support when a problem genuinely needs it, make day-to-day scope and sequencing calls within the documented playbook, and escalate only genuine exceptions.
 Delivery process. Improving the migration playbook as you run against it — tightening the plan, the checklists, and the handoffs so each acquisition goes faster and more predictably than the last.
 Who You Are: 
 You have 3–5 years project or program management, running implementation, migration or change management projects — ideally in B2B SaaS, professional services, or consulting. You ideally have managed multiple projects concurrently against firm deadlines..
 You are literate in Go-To-Market systems. You understand how a CRM and a support platform are put together and can scope a build, and hold a credible conversation with a founder about their GTM tech stack.
 You have directed the work of others — contractors, an agency pod, or junior admins — even without formal people management.
 A confident stakeholder-facing communicator. You’re a people person who can understand hesitant stakeholders and help them feel excited during a period of a lot of change.
 Strong judgment under ambiguity. You make defensible calls from a playbook instead of escalating everything, and you know which exceptions genuinely warrant escalation.
 A quality bar you set rather than inherit. You care how the build looks six months after go-live, not just at handoff.
 Strong written communication. Much of this job is a clear status update landing in the right inbox at the right time
 A bias for action. You would rather move something forward than perfect the plan
 The agility to adapt when a program changes shape mid-stream, and the confidence to get hands-on when it needs you
 Nice to Have: 
Formal project management training or certification (PMP or similar).
Familiar with project management tools (Asana, JIRA, Monday.com).
Hands-on CRM experience (HubSpot, Salesforce, PipeDrive, Zoho, etc.)
Hands-on Support experience (Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, etc.)
M&A exposure, particularly post-close systems consolidation.
Familiarity with migration tooling or scripting that moves data faster and more reliably than manual imports allow.
 Our Values at Beacon Software 
Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.
Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.
Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.
Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.
 How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role. 
 AI does not make hiring decisions: Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

az-ca-5961946485.description:
Escalon is a Toronto-based AI consultancy built by engineers. We help enterprises redesign their workflows around AI, then engineer, test and run those systems in production.
Our roots are in high-performance software, quality engineering and program delivery across gaming, SaaS and enterprise systems. That discipline is what makes AI hold up in the real world.
About the role
As a GTM Engineer you build the systems behind Escalon's growth: automated prospecting, lead enrichment and outreach workflows that put the right conversations in front of our team.
We are looking for a GTM operator who is also a hands-on builder. You understand how a revenue team works, you can turn its problems into working automations, and you have built those solutions yourself rather than only managing the tools and processes around them.
Our buyer and prospect signals live across a CRM, enrichment tools, outreach platforms, and public and third-party data. You will connect those sources, add context, and build workflows that show our team who to engage, why, when and with what message.
You do not need to be a traditional software engineer. You may come from revenue operations, sales operations, marketing operations, GTM systems or a similar technical GTM function. Because Escalon builds AI systems for clients, you will also be a first-hand user of the kind of AI workflows we recommend.
Clay CRM and workflow automation Lead enrichment Outreach tooling Data and integrations
What you'll do
Build prospecting and enrichment workflows: design and run automated account research, lead enrichment, scoring and prioritization that keep our pipeline full of the right companies and contacts.
Turn signals into action: connect and enrich data from the CRM, outreach tools, web activity and third-party sources to identify high-value accounts and recommend the next step.
Automate the GTM stack: build integrations and workflows across the CRM, Clay, sales engagement and outreach tools, enrichment providers and internal data sources.
Build agents and internal tools: use LLMs, APIs, webhooks, automation platforms and scripting to create tools that make our team faster and more effective.
Design outreach workflows: set up sequencing, personalization and follow-up, and keep them accurate, compliant with email and privacy rules, and well measured.
Prototype and iterate quickly: get solutions into users' hands, measure what works, and improve them from real feedback.
Make workflows reliable: add validation, guardrails, human review where it matters, monitoring and error handling so automations can be trusted in production.
Keep data clean: own data quality across tools so records, owners and statuses stay consistent as volume grows.
What you need
Experience in revenue operations, sales operations, GTM systems, marketing operations or a similar GTM function.
A solid understanding of B2B revenue workflows: lead management, routing, enrichment, qualification, account prioritization, prospecting and pipeline generation.
Hands-on experience building automations, integrations, internal tools or data workflows yourself.
Experience with GTM platforms such as Clay, a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce or similar), and outreach or sales engagement tools.
Experience building AI or LLM-powered workflows, with tools such as Claude, OpenAI, n8n, Zapier, Make or similar.
Comfort working with APIs, webhooks and scripting to connect systems.
The ability to work directly with the people who use your systems and translate their problems into working solutions.
Nice to have
Experience building account intelligence, scoring, routing or signal-based GTM workflows.
Experience taking an automation or AI workflow from prototype through production and adoption.
Experience in a consulting, services or other B2B environment with long sales cycles.

Responsable du marketing produit
 About AppDirect 
Become a digital, global citizen and enable the new generation of digital entrepreneurs around the world. AppDirect offers a subscription commerce platform to sell any product, through any channel, on any device - as a service. We power millions of subscriptions worldwide for organizations. We do this by our values-driven culture—one that enables you to Be Seen, Be Yourself, and Do Your Best Work.

You are a product marketer who has moved beyond execution and is ready to own a product line end to end. For this role, you will be the sole product marketing voice for the Business Unit. You need to be comfortable setting your own priorities and driving work forward without day-to-day direction. You translate competitive intelligence, win/loss data, and customer insight into clear positioning and concrete go-to-market plans that sales and product teams can act on. You understand how analyst relations work and you know how to work with customers to build advocacy and expansion-stage marketing programs. You are equally at home writing a sharp positioning narrative and reviewing pipeline data to assess whether your launches are working. Own the full go-to-market strategy for Business Unit’s Product launches, including positioning, success criteria, and cross-functional execution.
Define product marketing outcomes and success metrics tied to the Business Unit pipeline and new revenue targets, and track performance against them.
Partner directly with the Director of Product Management to shape the product roadmap using competitive intelligence, win/loss analysis, and market research.
Build and execute Business Unit's customer marketing strategy, with a focus on advocacy programs and expansion-stage motions that support cross-sell across AppDirect's unified monetization platform.
Own analyst relations for the Business Unit, including briefings, inquiries, and ongoing positioning with research firms such as Gartner.
Represent the product marketing perspective in cross-functional planning discussions with sales, customer success, and marketing leadership, translating business priorities into a clear product marketing roadmap.
Contribute to pricing analysis and provide recommendations to inform Business Unit's packaging and positioning decisions.
 What we're looking for 
3–5 years of product marketing experience in a B2B SaaS environment, with demonstrated ownership of go-to-market strategy.
Experience conducting competitive analysis, win/loss research, or market intelligence and using those findings to influence product or positioning decisions.
Familiarity with analyst relations processes, including preparing briefings and responding to research inquiries.
Experience developing customer marketing or expansion-stage programs (advocacy, upsell, or cross-sell campaigns).
Ability to work autonomously across multiple initiatives—this matters because you will be the primary product marketing owner for a Business Units and will set your own agenda without close oversight.
Clear, structured communication skills across written and verbal formats—this matters because you will regularly present positioning and strategy to sales leadership, product management, and executive stakeholders.
Experience with product-led growth (PLG) strategies is an asset, not a requirement.

About Clutch
We’re on a mission to reinvent the way people buy, sell, and own cars.
Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car buying and selling experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee... and that’s just the beginning.
Named two years in a row to the Globe & Mail’s list of the Top Growing Companies in Canada and also awarded spots on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50TM and Fast 500TM lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team.
Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including D1 Capital, Altos Ventures, BMO Capital Partners, Canaan, Real Ventures, and others. To learn more, visit clutch.ca.
About the role
We’re looking for a smart, resourceful, and analytically strong individual to join our Revenue team as Strategy and Operations Manager (Revenue). This role is an exceptional opportunity for someone early in their career 1-5 years post-grad who’s hungry to drive impact across a high-growth sales organization - working side by side with our VP of Sales on strategic initiatives, performance insights, and cross-functional projects that unlock growth.
What You’ll Do
Project-Based Execution
Lead and execute small to medium-sized strategic projects that drive incremental improvement across the sales team—ranging from process optimization to frontline tools to performance analysis.
Take ownership of project scoping, planning, execution, and results measurement—working across disciplines to see initiatives through end-to-end.
Ruthlessly prioritize initiatives that move the needle and align with broader revenue goals.
Work Cross-Functionally to Drive Change
Collaborate with Sales, Product, Marketing, Customer Experience, and Engineering to remove friction in the sales process and bring structure to ambiguity.
Be equally comfortable building a business case in Excel, presenting findings to the VP Sales, or jumping into a call with a distressed customer to understand root causes.
Translate complex problems into actionable insights—and ensure action happens.
Data-Driven Insights & Sales Strategy
Dive deep into sales and funnel data to uncover insights and opportunities. You’ll be expected to bring a strong analytical toolkit and be an 8+/10 when it comes to working with data.
Support forecasting, territory planning, performance dashboards, and root cause analysis to inform sales leadership decision-making.
Develop simple, clear, and persuasive recommendations backed by data and common sense.
Self-Learning & Experimentation
Take initiative to self-learn new tools, frameworks, and strategies—whether it’s mastering ChatGPT, learning how to write SQL, or figuring out how a new system works with minimal handholding.
Be proactive in experimenting with new ideas, rapidly testing assumptions, and applying learnings in real-time.
Develop comfort navigating ambiguity and unfamiliar territory—you’ll regularly tackle challenges that don’t come with a playbook.
What We’re Looking For
1-5 years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, sales strategy, business operations, or a high-performing startup environment.
8+/10 with data: Strong proficiency with Excel/Sheets required; experience with SQL, BI tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau)
Proven ability to lead structured projects and think strategically, while also rolling up your sleeves to get things done.
Comfortable with ambiguity and change—able to thrive in a fast-paced, ever-evolving environment.
Intellectually curious, fast learner, and someone who brings strong judgment and common sense to every conversation.
Strong communication and collaboration skills—you’re just as comfortable with execs as you are with frontline staff or developers.
Gritty, humble, and high-agency: you take initiative, own problems, and don’t wait to be told what to do.
Nice to Have
A genuine interest in Clutch’s industry—automotive, marketplaces, consumer tech, or the future of retail.
Passion for building things from the ground up and a desire to grow into a leadership role in the future.
Why Clutch
Partner directly with the VP Sales on initiatives that materially impact top-line performance.
Solve meaningful problems, fast: You’ll be in the room where decisions happen and have the chance to influence direction across the business.
Build your career: Whether your goal is GM, Product, Strategy, or Ops—this role sets a strong foundation for growth.
Competitive package: Market cash, equity upside, full benefits, and a collaborative in-office culture built on pace and curiosity.

Movable Ink scales content personalization for marketers through data-activated content generation and AI decisioning. Build and maintain scalable reporting that gives plan participants and leadership clear visibility into attainment, payouts, compensation expense, and plan performance.
Serve as the primary owner of compensation questions and issues, investigating discrepancies, identifying root causes, coordinating resolution across stakeholders, and communicating outcomes clearly to employees and business leaders.

Experience supporting the design, modeling, implementation, and administration of incentive compensation plans, with the ability to translate plan concepts into clear business rules and executable processes.
Experience with incentive compensation management software (CaptivateIQ strongly preferred) and CRM platforms (ideally Salesforce), with a strong understanding of how bookings, quotas, crediting, and organizational changes affect compensation outcomes.
Advanced Excel and/or Google Sheets skills, including complex calculations, large datasets, scenario modeling, and financial analysis.
Strong analytical skills and compensation controls expertise, including the ability to identify discrepancies, investigate root causes, implement durable solutions, and evaluate proposed plan changes for financial, operational, and behavioral implications.
Proven ability to lead cross‑functional projects, drive decisions across stakeholders without direct authority, and communicate complex compensation concepts clearly to participants, business leaders, and senior stakeholders.
Excellent organizational and project‑management skills, with a process‑improvement mindset, the ability to manage multiple compensation cycles and competing priorities, and a high degree of discretion when handling confidential information.

 Position Description 
The Global Incentive Compensation (GIC) team at Salesforce is a global leader for sales compensation in the technology industry. We manage the sales compensation for all Salesforce, end-to-end - from designing the sales compensation plan to enable the company’s go-to-market strategy to administering the payment so that our sales teams get paid on time. Within GIC, the Data Strategy team owns the foundational data architecture, data modeling, and secure data-sharing pipelines that power our global operational ecosystem (supporting $3B+ in annual commissions). We are hiring a Senior Technical Data Analyst to act as a key hands-on developer and business translator. This is a highly visible, active role. We are looking for an analyst who goes beyond simply executing transactional queries to designing and transforming data in our Snowflake Gold and Reporting database layers. You will serve as the ultimate operational bridge: partnering deeply with upstream business teams (Decision Analytics and Reporting) to run technical discovery, clarify business requirements, and then rolling up your sleeves to write production-grade SQL code to deliver clean, curated, and highly aggregated datasets to support complex reporting and high-priority, time sensitive ad-hoc business needs. Crucially, you are a natural 'data detective'. When the business requires data from unfamiliar or undocumented upstream systems, you will proactively hunt down the external business owners, ask the right investigative questions to decode their data structures, and document the requirements. You will build temporary technical workarounds in our Snowflake environment to keep the business agile, while carefully documenting the underlying technical gaps so they can be prioritized for permanent, long-term BT automation.
 Responsibilities 
 Gold & Reporting Layer Development: Actively develop, model, and optimize highly aggregated datasets, schemas, and tables in GIC's Snowflake Gold and Reporting layers. Transform cleaned, raw data sources into production-ready semantic models designed specifically to fuel BI tools and handle complex, high-priority ad-hoc business requests.
 Requirements Translation & Technical Discovery: Partner with business analysts in Reporting and Decision Analytics to run upfront discovery on new requests. Dissect vague requests, clarify and document clear business logic, and verify data feasibility in Snowflake before starting SQL development.
 Proactive Data Stewardship & Sourcing: Untangle unfamiliar, complex, or undocumented upstream data sources across the enterprise. Proactively hunt down the external business owners, ask the right investigative questions to decode their data structures, and establish GIC's technical stewardship over these newly discovered sources.
 Agile Data Curation & Gap Mitigation: Write intermediate SQL views and temporary workarounds in Snowflake to unblock urgent business decisions when upstream BT pipelines fall short. Ensure these agile data solutions are documented, clean, and easily maintainable.
 Technical Gap Documentation: Identify, translate, and document persistent upstream system and data gaps. Write clear technical specifications and schema requirements to hand off to GIC’s centralized leadership, who will strategically prioritize them on the Business Technology (BT) engineering roadmap.
 Project & Intake Coordination: Manage the intake, tracking, and prioritization of incoming data requests. Act as the primary coordinator for the team's delivery queue, setting clear expectations with stakeholders regarding timelines, scope, and technical constraints.
 Data Documentation & Governance: Build and maintain comprehensive GIC data dictionaries, technical wikis (Confluence/Canvas), and SQL query templates to help downstream partners self-serve safely and reduce redundant requests.
 Qualifications 
 Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Systems, Finance, or a related quantitative field.
 Experience: 5+ years of experience as a Technical Data Analyst, Database Developer, or Technical Business Analys

Establish a consistent grant-operations framewor

Every day we help them develop critical mineral resources more sustainably, design and build better infrastructure, source renewable energy, and reduce their impact on the environment.
We operate in 145+ countries while proudly maintaining headquarters in New Zealand.

Reporting to the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO), the Senior Director, Revenue Enablement is an executive-facing leadership role accountable for designing, scaling, and executing our global enablement strategy across all go-to-market (GTM) teams and channels (DRAMP). Combining high-level strategic vision with operational execution, this role partners closely with the CRO, Revenue Leadership Team, and regional sales leaders to shape enablement priorities, build scalable field capability, and directly tie enablement investments to measurable revenue productivity and customer-facing effectiveness.

Define, govern, and continuously evolve the global enablement operating model aligned with corporate growth targets, while partnering with regional sales leaders to adapt playbooks and methodologies to local market dynamics and buyer behaviors without compromising global standards. 
Build, mentor, and inspire a high-performing, globally distributed enablement organization rooted in accountability, continuous learning, and cross-functional collaboration.

Architect an onboarding engine and continuous learning curriculum across all customer-facing roles to substantially accelerate time to value and reduce ramp times for new hires. 
Collaborate deeply with Product, Customer Experience (CX), Product Marketing, and Operations to ensure unified messaging, timely feedback, and synchronized go-to-market execution. 
Audit, optimize, and drive adoption across the enablement technology stack (Salesforce, LMS, DemandFarm, and cutting-edge AI and intelligence tools) to streamline workflows and maximize active selling time.

10+ years of progressive commercial, sales operations, or sales enablement experience within an enterprise B2B SaaS or technology environment.

Who we are
We are an IT solutions company at our core with an approach that has enabled a low to no customer churn record. Clients reviewing their experiences with us consider our approach as solution-driven and customer-focused. We offer a blend of standard cloud solutions services, custom application designs, and productivity solutions, all of which leverage the Microsoft 365 toolset.
Role summary
The Customer Success Lead plans, organizes, directs, controls and evaluates client-service operations, ensuring service quality and client satisfaction. Reporting to the COO, the role leads a team supporting acquisition, onboarding, projects, support engagements and recurring services. The Lead works with Sales, Finance, Product Development and delivery teams to translate client needs into coordinated action, clear communications and reliable follow-through .
Key responsibilities
Develop and implement operating policies, procedures, priorities and service standards. Hire, train and supervise staff within delegated authority; assign work, balance workloads and maintain coverage. Coach employees and associates, identify development needs, review work quality and assist with administrative or technical problems affecting client service.
Develop client action plans and provide service-management expertise in response to client needs. Support acquisition by gathering requirements and coordinating enquiries with Sales. Advise project teams and identify additional opportunities through existing-client calls, renewals and reviews. Represent the company in relevant business and industry organizations when authorized.
Direct onboarding from acquisition or agreement acceptance through service readiness. Coordinate kickoff meetings and Sales-to-delivery handovers; confirm scope, contacts, responsibilities, timelines and dependencies. Track actions to completion, resolve gaps with project and support teams, and evaluate onboarding against the agreed client-service plan.
Plan, administer and control assigned budgets for projects, contracts, equipment and supplies. Monitor expenditure and resource requirements within approved limits. Oversee standard quotations using approved pricing and templates; coordinate contracts, agreements and RFQ/RFP inputs, deadlines and reviews. Refer non-standard terms and commitments for authorized approval.
Direct development and implementation of service-quality assessment strategies. Run client status calls covering project and support progress, commitments, risks and next steps. Gather feedback and evaluate satisfaction; coordinate escalation owners and corrective actions, keep clients informed, and track resolution without making unapproved commercial or delivery commitments.
Direct recurring-service administration, including licence renewals and changes. Maintain renewal dates, client contacts and follow-up records; coordinate approvals with Sales, Finance and service owners. Ensure renewal communications, licence change notices and service disruption notices are accurate and timely, and track outstanding client actions.
Oversee client and billing enquiries. Investigate questions using agreements, quotations, licence and service records; coordinate clarification and resolution with Finance and delivery teams. Keep clients informed, track closure and identify recurring issues. Invoice adjustments, credits, refunds and payment-term changes remain subject to approval by the authorized function.
Advise Product Development using structured client and industry insights, recurring needs, service issues and product gaps. Direct implementation of approved product and service playbooks through team workflows, templates, training and handovers. Monitor adoption, document exceptions and recommend improvements without promising unapproved roadmap features or release dates.
Exercise budget, hiring and commercial authority only within delegated limits . Escalate decisions outside those limits to authorized approvers and obtain required approvals before issuing commitments or changing commercial terms .

Related degree or college diploma, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Five or more years of progressive experience in Customer Success, Client Services, Sales Support, Account Operations or Project Coordination, including team leadership and client-service management.
Strong communication, organization and follow-through, with the ability to manage competing priorities and collaborate across commercial and delivery teams.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and CRM platforms such as Dynamics CRM or HubSpot.
Technology services, managed services, consulting, partner-program or licensing experience is an asset.

Benefits package including health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off.

We’re financing the future of energy
Crux is the capital platform for the clean economy. We modernize capital raising and deployment for clean energy and critical infrastructure with solutions across advisory, investments, technology, and intelligence.
Our team of 120+ is composed of experts in energy, tax, finance, government, and technology. We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Overture, Ardent Venture Partners, QED, Canapi, and others. These funds are joined by strategic investors including Pattern Energy, Clearway Energy, EDF Renewables, Intersect Power, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.
An inflection point in American energy and manufacturing
Energy demand is growing for the first time in decades, driving an urgent need for more affordable and reliable electricity. More electricity requires new clean energy infrastructure and strong domestic supply chains for minerals and components, as well as large amounts of capital.
Traditionally project financing is opaque, fragmented, and analog. At Crux, we’re changing that. Through unmatched insights and expertise, white-glove service, purpose-built tools, and risk underwriting, we power a more prosperous, clean, and secure energy future.
We are scaling quickly and looking for team members who are eager to combine deep expertise with an AI- and tech-forward mindset.
The Role
We’re hiring a HubSpot & Revenue Systems Lead to join our Revenue Operations team. HubSpot is the system of record for how Crux runs its commercial business across Transferable Tax Credits, Debt, and Investments: deals, listings, buyer orders, and the reporting leadership uses to make decisions. It has grown quickly alongside the business, and it now needs a dedicated owner.
This role owns HubSpot end to end. You’ll clean up and streamline what exists today, define how new products and business lines get built into the system, and use AI to design the commercial systems Crux will need as it scales. This is a builder’s seat, not a ticket queue. It requires understanding how deals actually move, earning trust with commercial teams who live in the system every day, and having a point of view on what good looks like.
What You’ll Do
Own HubSpot as Crux’s commercial system of record: objects, pipelines, properties, permissions, integrations, and data quality
Audit and streamline the current setup, retiring redundant fields, workflows, and workarounds so the system is simpler to use and easier to trust
Define the data model and processes for new products and business lines as they launch, working with commercial leads to translate how a deal actually works into how it’s captured
Make AI a core part of how the system is built and run: agents and automations for enrichment, data hygiene, deal and listing updates, routing, and alerts
Build AI-powered tools on top of our commercial data, such as deal summaries, pipeline reviews, and self-serve answers for commercial teams, so people spend less time updating the CRM and more time on deals
Shape the future-state architecture for how HubSpot, our analytics layer (Omni), and internal tools fit together, with AI designed in from the start rather than bolted on
Partner with AI-Native Ops and Product on tooling, owning the requirements and the outcome rather than handing problems off
Train and support commercial teams so the system gets used the way it’s designed, and adjust the design when it isn’t
Maintain documentation so how the system works doesn’t live in one person’s head
What You Bring
4–8 years of professional experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or business systems roles.
Hands‑on HubSpot administration experience, including custom objects and associations, multiple

ht together a team that are experts in clean energy finance, and the best technologies. Use your expertise while getting to be on the cutting edge of applying AI to your day and your clients’ experience.

Job Details
 Company: ShareGate
 Position: GTM Engineering - ShareGate
 Location: Canada - Remote
About ShareGate
ShareGate is the leading Microsoft 365 migration and governance platform, trusted by over 100,000 IT pros for its unmatched simplicity.
It offers the simplest, most reliable, and most affordable way to move business data to Microsoft 365.
Whether migrating from Google Workspace, file shares, Exchange Online, SharePoint On-Premises, or tenant-to-tenant, ShareGate gets the job done, without surprises. From cloud transformation to M&A integration, it keeps things just damn simple.
ShareGate also helps organizations stay in control once their data is migrated. Its powerful governance features let users assess environments, uncover issues, and apply fixes on the spot, so everything stays clean, secure, and optimized. It lays the groundwork for safe Microsoft Copilot deployment within organizations.
ShareGate is developed by Workleap Technologies, a Montréal‑based software company.
Your role
ShareGate’s customers generate rich signals (product usage, support interactions, renewal dates), but those signals aren’t yet connected into an engine that protects and grows the revenue we already have. As our GTM Architect, Expansion & Retention, you’ll design, build and ship AI agents and agentic workflows that turn those signals into saved renewals and cross-sell pipeline. This is an embedded engineering role within GTM, not back-office ops: you’ll apply the signal-based, agent-first approach we already use for new customer acquisition to the customers we already have.
Your impact:
Protect renewals by building AI agents that continuously monitor renewal health and flag at‑risk accounts to Account Managers early, with context, recommended next steps and enough lead time to act.
Grow revenue from our existing customers by designing and running an agentic cross-sell motion: score fit for our second product line, research each account, personalize outreach, qualify interest and route genuine intent to the right salesperson with the full context needed to close.
Define the signals your agents need and partner with Revenue Systems, which builds and owns the data flow between product usage and the CRM. Validate the data with SQL before you act on it.
Replace manual workflows with AI agents and reusable pipeline modules (not one‑off automations) that Account Management and Sales can run and own on their own.
Tune both motions by owning reporting on pipeline generated, conversion, renewal outcomes and revenue impact, and by running controlled experiments without adding headcount.
Drive adoption by turning everything you build into SOPs, demos and playbooks, so the team uses what you ship, not just appreciates it.
Your team
You’ll join a GTM engineering effort that already runs a signal-based, agent-first approach to new customer acquisition, and now points it at the customers we already have. The challenge: connect usage, support and renewal signals into agents that reduce the friction between signal and action. The tools, plays and channels will evolve; that mission won’t.
Our stack: low-code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), Python or TypeScript, SQL on our data warehouse, and our CRM (HubSpot).
What you'll bring
Background in RevOps, GTM/marketing operations, customer success operations or GTM engineering, with hands‑on experience building automation;
Hands‑on experience with low‑code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), plus working knowledge of Python or TypeScript for API integrations and data transformation;
fluency with agentic tools and MCP connectors. Strong LLM workflow design (agent orchestration, tool use, evaluation), sound judgment on when AI adds leverage versus complexity, and a track record of shipping AI agents or LLM workflows to real users, not just prototypes;
Working SQL to query and validate usage, support and renewal data., so you can build and trust the data behind your agents;
CRM fluency (HubSpot a plus): enough to design agents on our data model and work with Revenue Systems on what you need.
Understanding of subscription business metrics (renewal rate, net retention, customer li
[...]
ification or scoring systems; a B2B SaaS background with multiple product lines, ideally product‑led or demo‑led; published technical content that makes complex systems accessible.
What the job comes with
Base salary: $110,000 - $140,000. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
OTE: $120,000 - $155,000
LTIP program, share in Workleap's long‑term growth.
RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
Flexible vacation policy.
Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
In‑person gathering twice a year.
Claude access, for everyone.
Note: The internal title for this role is GTM Architect.
What drives us
We build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.
We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.
If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.
How we hire
Transparency is how we hire - for you as much as for us.
Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take‑home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly - your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.
We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.
We can't wait to meet you.

fluency with agentic tools and MCP connectors. Strong LLM workflow design (agent orchestration, tool use, evaluation), sound judgment on when AI adds leverage versus complexity, and a track record of shipping AI agents or LLM workflows to real users, not just prototypes;

CRM fluency (HubSpot a plus): enough to design agents on our data model and work with Revenue Systems on what you need.
Understanding of subscription business metrics (renewal rate, net retention, customer lifetime value), and experience with or strong interest in outbound and signal‑based go‑to‑market motions;

scoring systems; a B2B SaaS background with multiple product lines, ideally product‑led or demo‑led; published technical content that makes complex systems accessible.

OTE: $120,000 - $155,000

About ShareGate
ShareGate is the leading Microsoft 365 migration and governance platform, trusted by over 100,000 IT pros for its unmatched simplicity.
It offers the simplest, most reliable, and most affordable way to move business data to Microsoft 365.
Whether migrating from Google Workspace, file shares, Exchange Online, SharePoint On-Premises, or tenant-to-tenant, ShareGate gets the job done, without surprises. From cloud transformation to M&A integration, it keeps things just damn simple.
ShareGate also helps organizations stay in control once their data is migrated. Its powerful governance features let users assess environments, uncover issues, and apply fixes on the spot, so everything stays clean, secure, and optimized. It lays the groundwork for safe Microsoft Copilot deployment within organizations.
ShareGate is developed by Workleap Technologies, a Montréal‑based software company.
Your role
ShareGate's customers generate rich signals (product usage, support interactions, renewal dates), but those signals aren't yet connected into an engine that protects and grows the revenue we already have. As our GTM Developer, Expansion & Retention, you'll design, build and ship AI agents and agentic workflows that turn those signals into saved renewals and cross-sell pipeline. This is an embedded engineering role within GTM, not back-office ops: you'll apply the signal-based, agent-first approach we already use for new customer acquisition to the customers we already have.
Your impact:
Protect renewals by building AI agents that continuously monitor renewal health and flag at-risk accounts to Account Managers early, with context, recommended next steps and enough lead time to act.
Grow revenue from our existing customers by designing and running an agentic cross-sell motion: score fit for our second product line, research each account, personalize outreach, qualify interest and route genuine intent to the right salesperson with the full context needed to close.
Own the data flow between our product usage systems and our CRM so that renewal risk scoring and cross-sell targeting are accurate and trustworthy, including data quality, sender reputation and attribution accuracy.
Replace manual workflows with AI agents and reusable pipeline modules (not one-off automations) that Account Management and Sales can run and own on their own.
Tune both motions by owning reporting on pipeline generated, conversion, renewal outcomes and revenue impact, and by running controlled experiments without adding headcount.
Drive adoption by turning everything you build into SOPs, demos and playbooks, so the team uses what you ship, not just appreciates it.
Your team
You will join a GTM engineering effort that already runs a signal‑based, agent‑first approach to new customer acquisition, and now points it at the customers we already have. The challenge: connect usage, support and renewal signals into agents that reduce the friction between signal and action. The tools, plays and channels will evolve; that mission won’t.
Our stack
low‑code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), Python or TypeScript, SQL on our data warehouse, and our CRM (HubSpot).
What you'll bring
Background in RevOps, GTM/marketing operations, customer success operations or GTM engineering, with hands‑on experience building automation;
Hands‑on experience with low‑code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), plus working knowledge of Python or TypeScript for API integrations and data transformation;
fluency with agentic tools and MCP connectors. Strong LLM workflow design (agent orchestration, tool use, evaluation), sound judgment on when AI adds leverage versus complexity, and a track record of shipping AI agents or LLM workflows to real users, not just prototypes;
Working SQL to query and validate usage, support and renewal data., so you can build and trust the data behind your agents;
RevOps systems depth: strong CRM fluency and data modeling (HubSpot experience is a plus), clean integrations between product usage data and the CRM, and deliverability management for outbound;
Understanding of subscription business metrics (renewal rate, net retention, customer lifetime value), and experience with or strong interest in outbound and signal‑based go‑to‑market motions;
The ability to work directly with Sales and Account Management, translate complex builds into plain language, and earn adoption through demos and handoff docs, without a PM to bridge the gap;
Bonus: experience building AI‑driven qualification or scoring systems; a B2B SaaS background with multiple product lines, ideally product‑led or demo‑led; published technical content that makes complex systems accessible.
Most of this sounds like you?
What the job comes with
Base salary: $110,000 - $140,000. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions. OTE

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.
We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

Product philosophy
Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.
Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.
Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.
Our vision
We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.
But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.
Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.
In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.
Our traction
Since 2020, we’ve generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com website.
More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.
Our team
Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.

Our partners either use the platform APIs directly or work with us to develop applications for their use cases. 
 BetterLetter , our AI tool helping practices decrease their admin burden in processing clinical letters. ackstop Act as backup for the VP Business Operations, keeping things moving when they are away or at capacity, within agreed decision-making and spending limits. Take on ad hoc projects as priorities change.

Hello, we're Laka
You might not have heard of us yet - that's OK, you've found us now - come and find out more about our journey...
Founded in 2017, Laka set out to transform insurance by connecting passionate cyclists to form a collective and protect their bikes for when things go wrong - a better model for insurance was born. For once people come first in insurance by fairly sharing the cost amongst each other. We exist to rewrite the rules of insurance so it’s something people stand with, not against.
Our model: Laka makes sure everything runs smoothly for The Collective - from exceptionally fast claims, splitting the cost fairly, guaranteeing a maximum price and all the other heavy lifting of a regulated insurance business. For that service, the collective pays Laka a fee relative to the claims in a month.
Take a closer look at exactly what this means and how it works here.
What have we been up to since then...?
In a nutshell, we've been very busy! Here are a few of the massive achievements we've had:
 Raised an awesome Series B investment round
 Grown the team to over 60 Lakanauts, based across the UK, NL and France, enabling a choice-based, hybrid way of working
 Launched Laka in a total of 11 countries, essentially helping more people in more places!
 Captured the UK, NL and French enthusiast cyclist market and expanded into commercial business partnering
 Been awarded 'Best Cycle Insurance Provider' (for the past 8 years in a row - go us! )
 Opened 3 shiny new offices in London, Bristol & Amsterdam to provide spaces for people to collaborate as they like
 We've also achieved a 5* rating on Google Reviews and Glassdoor - go check us out!
Help us continue to change an outdated industry...
We’re growing fast on our path to make the Laka collective model the industry standard and we’re expanding across segments, products, and territories. We’re looking for innovative, bold and brave minds to help us build the world’s best insurance company.
 The Commercial Operations Analyst role

Our CS Operations team, part of our broader Customer Operations team, strives to help our Customer Success organization scale and grow faster. This function will act as a key business partner to the leaders of our Customer Success team. Your responsibilities will range across a variety of strategic initiatives including piloting and scaling up new projects, analyzing data to come up with meaningful business insights, and optimizing processes. We are looking for an experienced professional to help us lead this global team. You will be responsible for learning the ins and outs of MongoDB’s Customer Success function, play a critical role in building relationships with the senior leadership team, and drive forward initiatives that will help us unlock sales revenue. The ideal candidate understands what makes our Customers successful and makes a Field team thrive, has a strong interest in analyzing data to understand the business and drive impact, and thrives in shaping narratives that are conducive to helping our teams grow.
We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Dublin for our hybrid working model.
The Opportunity
As a Manager of Customer Success Operations, you will:
Lead a team of analytical and operational business partners that are aligned to the CS organization
Drive the operating rhythm of our business including monthly and quarterly business reviews, forecasting, org deep dives, and ongoing business planning efforts (including contributing to headcount and capacity planning, account and territory assignments, etc.)
Partner with Senior CS and Operations leadership to drive market and segment-specific analyses to uncover insight, influence key decisions, and shape the longer-term vision of the team
Independently run forecasting and business review calls
Derive understanding and insights on emerging trends from our data and present recommendations on how we can drive better outcomes to CS leadership
Influence the data and systems strategy and processes required to scale commercial teams
Become well-versed in our sales KPIs and their implications on performance tracking,compensation and forecasting
Conceptualize and pilot new programs to test the effectiveness of various CS workflows, structures, and decisions
Collaborate with various business units to drive productivity and headcount scenario analyses
Qualifications
Bachelor’s Degree with a quantitative focus (Economics, Finance, Computer Science, Mathematics, etc.)
5+ years of work experience in either CS, Sales, GTM Strategy and/or Operations
1+ years of leadership experience
Comfortable being in a player-coach manager type role
Familiarity with consumption-based software business models
Experience as a business partner to a field organization
Experience with at least one major business intelligence tool (Tableau, Google Data Studio, Looker)
The Ideal Candidate
Thrives in working in a fast-paced working environment
Effective communicator who can break down convoluted technical, financial, or operational concepts into simple business vernacular
Believes that the best way to drive success is by motivating and leveraging their team to deliver results without being hands-off or disconnected from the day to day work
You’re intensely curious. You want to know how things work, and you want to know why, and you’re comfortable getting your hands dirty in data and process to get there
You love analysis and iteration and optimization - you’re never satisfied with how things are, because you can always see ways to make things better.
You are a spreadsheet wizard with the ability to manipulate and analyze data
You can navigate your way around Salesforce with relative ease

experience in freight forwarding or international transport;

strong commercial skills, analytical ability and negotiation skills;
excellent communication skills and the ability to connect with different stakeholders;
fluent business English, both written and spoken.

a gross monthly salary between €4,500 and €6,000;
a bonus;
a 5% annual gratification;
a lease car.

 DSV – Global transport and logistics 
 What moves you? 
At DSV, we move more than goods. We move careers, ambitions and opportunities.
With close to 150,000 colleagues in over 90 countries, we are the global leader in transport and logistics, and it is our people who bring our services and solutions to life every day. From frontline operations to business functions, every role contributes to keeping supply chains flowing and societies running.
Here, you are trusted to take ownership, act on your ideas and make decisions that create real impact. It is a place where people, careers and ideas keep moving forward.  Start here. Go anywhere

About the role and team 
This is a new role, creating a new capability for Uber Eats in EMEA.
A single investment vehicle owns a portfolio of QSR and Casual Dining brands operating across multiple EMEA markets. Today, Uber's relationship with that portfolio is managed market by market. This role changes that: it establishes a single, EMEA-wide operational capability that sits above the individual markets and owns the portfolio end to end.
As the Customer Success Manager for EMEA Enterprise Accounts, you will be the connective tissue between the fund's HQ, the leadership of each of its brands, and Uber Eats' commercial teams across EMEA. You'll map to and own the most senior HQ relationships, build the standardised reporting and QBR cadence the portfolio has never had, and — critically — turn Uber's data into decision-grade insight that helps these brands decide which markets to enter next, where to put their next store, which customer segments to target, and which brands to acquire.
You will work alongside a dedicated analyst, so you don't need to build the queries yourself. What you do need is the judgement to know which question is worth asking, the rigour to interrogate what the data actually says, and the presence to land the resulting recommendation with a brand CEO and with a sophisticated finance team at an investment fund.
This is a build role. You will be designing the playbook as you run it, working in close partnership with Account Managers in each market and with the EMEA Enterprise Director. 
 What you’ll do 
Build durable relationships with the most senior HQ contacts accountable across all EMEA markets 
Establish Uber Eats as the default strategic partner at HQ level, not only at market level
Design and run a standardised EMEA-level QBR for the portfolio.
Build consistent, comparable reporting by brand and by market, giving HQ a single view of performance across the portfolio.
Own cross-market prospect pipeline management, giving HQ and local teams a shared and accurate view of what's live, what's landing and what's next.
Set the analytical agenda for the account and direct the work of a dedicated analyst. Become an extension of the Partner’s strategy team, answering questions such as which market to enter next, where to open the next store, which Customer Segment to target and how to optimise menu pricing strategy
Interpret complex datasets, draw conclusions and convert them into clear, defensible recommendations that HQ and local teams can act on.
Present those recommendations credibly to brand C-Suite and to investment-fund finance professionals.
Drive knowledge sharing and best-practice standardisation across markets, so a win in one country becomes the default in the next.
Coordinate cross-market prospecting and ensure the portfolio experiences one seamless, joined-up Uber.
Work closely with Account Managers in each market and with the Director across the account, aligning them behind a single portfolio plan.
Win merchant sentiment through elevated, consistent service. Be the partner's advocate inside Uber and Uber's advocate inside the partner.
Act as a core member of the deal team on EMEA-level commercial agreements aimed at winning new markets, securing preferential terms and establishing Uber Eats as the preferred partner across the portfolio.
Build the commercial case, shape the strategy and supply the analysis and partner insight that underpin the negotiation, working with Legal, Finance and local commercial leadership.
Define the operating model, cadence and playbook for EMEA Enterprise account management — and make it repeatable for the next portfolio after this one.
 Basic Qualifications 
6+ years' experience in account management, customer success, strategic partnerships, commercial strategy, consulting or a comparable client-facing role.
Demonstrable experience owning senior, multi-stakeholder relationships, including at C-Suite or equivalent level.
Strong analytical judgement: able to interpret complex data, stress-test the conclusions and turn them into a clear, well-argued recommendation.
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the credibility to hold the room with both 
[...]
s.
Experience working across multiple markets or through matrixed, in-market teams.
 Preferred Qualifications 
Experience in QSR, Casual Dining, restaurant, retail, FMCG or delivery/marketplace businesses.
Experience working with private equity or investment funds, or with portfolio-level stakeholders, and fluency with the metrics they care about.
Experience contributing to complex, multi-market commercial negotiations as part of a deal team.
Experience directing or partnering with analytical resource to produce client-facing insight.
Comfort operating with ambiguity and defining structure where none exists.

About the role and team 
Uber’s Commercial Enablement team equips commercial teams across EMEA with the capabilities, tools, and knowledge needed to acquire the selection that matters, build successful merchant partnerships, and drive sustainable growth.
As the EMEA Enablement Lead Acquisition, you will own the ongoing capability development of Account Executives across the region. You will develop a deep understanding of their day-to-day responsibilities, from identifying and engaging prospective merchants to diagnosing business needs, negotiating sustainable agreements, and ensuring a strong handoff into merchant onboarding.
Working within the Sales Excellence pod, you will identify challenges shared across acquisition teams and translate them into structured learning programs, practical workshops, and scalable resources. You will connect global sales methodology with regional business priorities and local market realities, helping AEs progress from foundational knowledge to confident, advanced execution throughout their careers.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role combining commercial expertise, program ownership, facilitation, and stakeholder partnership. Approximately 20% of the role will focus on equipping acquisition managers to reinforce skills and develop their teams.
 What you’ll do 
Own the EMEA acquisition capability roadmap: Partner with Acquisition leaders, Commercial Operations, and Global Enablement to identify the skills most important to regional business priorities. Translate these needs into a clear, prioritized development plan across acquisition segments.
Become a trusted expert in the AE role: Stay close to sellers through shadowing, call reviews, field observation, and regular engagement with market teams. Understand how AEs prospect, prioritize opportunities, build merchant relationships, manage their pipeline, and close business.
Turn recurring challenges into structural solutions: Combine field feedback, seller observations, and commercial data to identify capability gaps affecting multiple teams or markets. Build, pilot, and scale practical solutions, distinguishing learning needs from process, tooling, or policy issues that require another owner.
Build continuous development journeys: Adapt and extend global competency frameworks into clear EMEA learning pathways, with primary ownership of Skilled (200) and Advanced (300) development. Connect these pathways with foundational onboarding to create continuity throughout an AE’s time at Uber.
Lead acquisition academies and workshops: Own the regional design, planning, delivery, and improvement of programs covering pipeline generation, solution selling, merchant financials, and deal execution and negotiation. Tailor depth and application to different seller experience levels and commercial segments.
Make learning practical and relevant: Develop realistic merchant scenarios, role plays, deal simulations, call examples, and field assignments. Create accessible playbooks, discovery guides, negotiation preparation tools, and business case templates that sellers can apply in their daily work.
Equip acquisition managers to develop their teams: Build managers’ capability to observe selling behaviors, assess skills, provide actionable feedback, and reinforce learning through call reviews, deal reviews, and regular coaching. Align these resources with the Expansion Enablement Lead to maintain consistent manager development standards.
Connect regional consistency with local relevance: Partner with market stakeholders and the Enablement Delivery pod to adapt examples, language, and facilitation to local needs while preserving common learning standards. Bring market feedback and proven practices into regional programs and share relevant improvements with Global Enablement.
Collaborate across Enablement functions: Provide acquisition expertise to GTM & Activation, Tech & Productivity, and Retail & Direct initiatives where seller skills are required. Agree clear responsibilities and deliverables with the relevant lead and mobilize shared delivery capacity according to priorities.

Professional proficiency in an additional EMEA language.

 About Avari 
 Avari is a fast-growing short-term rental property management company, operating in partnership with Casago across Florida's Gulf Coast, Alabama, Utah, Nevada, Oregon, and the Lake Tahoe region of California. As we continue to expand through strategic acquisitions and new market growth, we help homeowners maximize the value of their vacation rental investments through exceptional management and proven returns.
