As a Sales Operations Associate with Avari Management, this role sits at the intersection of data and the field. You'll mine market-level data to surface homeowner-acquisition opportunities in our priority markets, translate those insights into clear messaging and collateral for our reps, and provide the sales operations backbone — quota tracking, payouts, and forecasting support — that keeps the team running.
In short: you turn "here's what the data says" into "here's exactly what our reps should say and send," and you keep the numbers behind the sales team honest and current. You're happiest with a lot of surface area, moving fast, and a mix of analysis, communication, and operations in a single week.v
 What you'll do 
 Market intelligence & analysis 
Mine internal and third-party data (CRM, data warehouse, STR market data, property/ownership records) to identify high-opportunity markets, owner segments, and competitive dynamics.
Build repeatable market profiles covering owner density, competitor presence, pricing, seasonality, and regulatory considerations.
Partner with RevOps on enrichment workflows so the data feeding the field stays accurate and current.
 Messaging & collateral 
Translate market insights into clear value propositions tailored by market and owner segment.
Create rep-ready collateral: one-pagers, outreach/email templates, call scripts, market briefs, and objection-handling guides.
Keep the content library organized so reps can find and use what they need.
 Sales enablement & adoption 
Equip BD/sales reps with the market playbooks, messaging, and collateral they need to win owners in each region.
Onboard and train reps on positioning, tooling, and plays, and drive real adoption — not just published assets.
Run feedback loops with reps to learn what's landing in-market and refine accordingly.
 Sales operations support 
Track quota attainment across the sales team and calculate commission/payouts accurately and on time.
Support forecasting and pipeline reporting, including operating the team's pipeline-weighting and projected-revenue reporting.
Maintain CRM hygiene and build reporting that connects rep activity and enablement to pipeline and owner signings.
 What you'll bring 
 Required 
3–4 years in sales/revenue operations, sales enablement, analytics, growth, or another data-forward GTM role.
 Strong with data — you pull, analyze, and interpret it without hand-holding. Fluent in spreadsheets and CRM, and quick to pick up SQL or BI tools.
 Tech-native — you learn new tools fast and instinctively look for ways to automate and streamline.
 Communicate insights well — you turn a dataset into a clear, persuasive narrative and into material a rep can actually use.
 High energy and pace — you thrive with lots of moving parts, ambiguity, and a fast tempo, and you take ownership without waiting to be told.
Comfort with numbers behind a sales team: quota, commissions/payouts, and forecasting mechanics (or a clear aptitude to ramp quickly).
 Preferred 
Experience in proptech, real estate, hospitality, marketplaces, franchise/multi-location, or other geographically segmented go-to-market models.
HubSpot and/or data-warehouse (e.g., Snowflake) experience.
Familiarity with prospecting/enrichment tooling (e.g., Clay) and STR or local-market data sources.
Exposure to owner-, SMB-, or B2B2C-acquisition motions.
 What success looks like 
 First 90 days: market profiles for the top [3–5] priority markets, a first rep-facing playbook in market, and clean, reliable quota/attainment reporting the team trusts.
 First 6–12 months: measurable rep adoption of collateral, demonstrable conversion lift in enabled markets, and a repeatable "market → messaging → enablement" motion — with sales ops reporting running like clockwork.
 Compensation & benefits 
Base salary range: $85,000 – $100,000, depending on experience.
Performance bonus: 15% target annual bonus (bringing target total compensation to approximately $98,000–$115,000+, depending on base salary and performance).
Health, dental, vision, 401(k) match, unlimited PTO & remote-first culture.
Professional development and career growth opportunities

Position 
Senior Customer Success Engineer
 Reports to 
Tech Ops Team Lead
 Location 
Remote, US, Eastern Time Zone Only.
 Employment 
Full-time
 Salary Range 
$140,000-$175,000 (based on location and experience) + equity
 Why this role exists 
Dataro is an ethically minded SaaS startup using machine learning to help nonprofits raise more money and do more good. Our platform powers fundraising for organizations around the world, helping them run smarter campaigns and build better relationships with their donors.
Every day we ingest and process hundreds of millions of records from a wide range of fundraising and CRM systems. That data underpins everything we do.
This role sits where that data meets our customers, primarily in the UK, as well as across North America. You'll be the technical point of contact as customers onboard and as issues come up, making sure their data flows cleanly into our platform and that problems get resolved quickly. When customers can trust their data, they can focus on what matters: raising money for their cause.
 What you'll work on 
 Resolving customer technical issues. Our technical support team handles first-line tickets. You'll take on L2 issues: investigating data and integration problems, resolving what you can directly, and escalating to our engineering team in Australia when an issue needs a code-level fix. Because Sydney is offline during most of your day, you'll own each escalation end to end: keeping the customer informed, putting workarounds in place where possible, and documenting the issue clearly enough that an engineer can act on it overnight without follow-up questions.
 Onboarding and integrations. You'll sit with customers to understand their CRM, their data structures, and how their fundraising team actually works, then write the Python and SQL that turns their data into something our models can use. Where you spot repeated manual work, you'll have room to automate it.
 Working across teams. You'll run technical calls with customers and explain constraints to people who aren't engineers. You'll keep CSMs informed on progress, flag risk early, and help document how onboarding and support work so that knowledge is shared across the team.
 Handling sensitive data. You'll work with donor data every day, including personal information. We're SOC 2 certified and support GDPR requirements through regional hosting and strict data residency controls. You'll handle that data with the same care.
 What you'll bring 
Senior here means you can own a customer issue from first report to resolution without hand-holding, and work independently with your engineering team 14-16 hours ahead.
3+ years in a customer-facing technical role, such as solutions engineering, implementation, technical support, or data consulting
An AI-native way of working: you use AI tools to build, debug, and automate in your day-to-day work
Strong SQL, with real comfort in large datasets
Confident Python for data work, automation, and scripting
Confidence with APIs: authenticating, paging through results, and debugging a failing integration from the logs
Working knowledge of AWS and Git
A methodical approach to troubleshooting: you can reproduce an issue, isolate the cause, and write it up so an engineer can act on it
Excellent communication, including leading technical customer calls and keeping customers informed while an issue is being resolved
Good judgment in triage: you can assess competing tickets and requests, decide what's urgent, and explain why
A track record of working independently and owning problems end to end
 Bonus points 
Implementation, forward-deployed, or consulting-style engineering experience
Experience with fundraising or nonprofit CRMs such as Salesforce, NXT, and Blackbaud, or other nonprofit sector experience
Experience with DuckDB or AWS Athena
Experience with a support ticketing system and formal escalation processes
Experience working with distributed teams across time zones
 What makes this exciting 
Your work directly helps nonprofits raise more money for the causes they serve. Every integration you build and every issue you resolve means a fundraising team can spend less time fighting their data and more time connecting with donors.
You'll also work across a wide range of CRM systems and data setups, which gives you a rare, end-to-end view of how our platform meets the real world. And you'll work closely with customers, CSMs, and engineers across the US, UK, and Australia.
 What we offer 
100% coverage of employee health, dental, and vision insurance, with employer contribution toward dependent coverage
HSA Plan Option with employer contribution
401(k) with employer contribution
Company equity
Paid Holidays, Vacation, & Sick Leave
Paid Parental Leave
 Working hours 
You'll work 8am to 4pm Eastern Time and must be based in the Eastern Time Zone. Our customers are primarily in the UK, so your mornings overlap with their afternoons, giving you about four hours of shared working time with the UK team. Expect the occasional earlier start for a UK customer call, and the odd call with our engineering team in Sydney, Australia.
During your first 2-3 weeks, your working day will shift later to overlap with our Australian team for onboarding and training. Sydney's business day starts in the late afternoon to evening Eastern Time, so expect evening hours during this period. After training, you'll move to your standard schedule.

About us: 
Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets through automating and streamlining the work of assurance and audit practitioners specifically within cybersecurity, privacy, and ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance). Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.
We’re based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We're backed by top investors including Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Eric Ries, and more.
We value diversity — in backgrounds and in experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide’s team is inclusive, driven, humble and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture that we are building, seeking teammates that are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.
As an early-stage start-up employee, you’ll have the opportunity to build out the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners’ lives easier by eliminating up to 50% of their work and giving them better work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you will find a home at Fieldguide.
 About the role: 
Fieldguide is seeking a Sales Enablement Manager to join our growing sales enablement team. As our dedicated enablement lead for Corporate Internal Audit (IA) and Public Sector, you'll play a crucial role in shaping and elevating the performance of the sellers who cover these segments. This position offers a unique opportunity to build and implement segment-specific enablement strategies from the ground up, directly impacting Fieldguide's growth trajectory as we expand beyond CPA and advisory firms into corporate audit functions and government buyers.
In this role, you'll be the driving force behind our sales team's success in these markets, creating and delivering targeted training programs, developing critical sales content, and serving as a trusted advisor to our Account Executives. Your expertise in sales methodologies and in how corporate and public sector organizations buy will be instrumental in optimizing our sales processes and enhancing our team's effectiveness in a competitive market.
 What you'll do: 
Enhance our current sales enablement programs, including new hire onboarding and ongoing training initiatives, with dedicated tracks for Corporate IA and Public Sector
Develop and deliver content for sales training, covering industry knowledge, product expertise, and sales methodologies, including internal audit frameworks and standards and public sector compliance frameworks
Serve as the company's expert on sales methodology (MEDDPICC), ensuring effective implementation across the sales organization
Develop Public Sector buying-process enablement: RFP/RFI/RFQ response, fiscal-year and budget-cycle timing, procurement vehicles and other relevant requirements
Build Corporate IA buyer enablement
Conduct regular 1:1 sessions with Account Executives, providing personalized coaching grounded in real call review and driving adoption of best practices
Collaborate closely with marketing to align sales enablement efforts with broader company messaging and initiatives, including events and associations relevant to these segments
Analyze team performance metrics by segment to identify areas for improvement and develop targeted enablement strategies
Stay current on industry trends, regulatory changes, government budget cycles, and competitors to inform and enhance our sales approach
 About you: 
5-7+ years of experience in sales enablement in a B2B SaaS environment, preferably vertical SaaS, with direct experience enabling teams that sell to enterprise and/or public sector buyers
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Business, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent work experience
Deep expertise in sales methodologies, particularly MEDDPICC/MEDDIC, and applying them to complex, multi-stakeholder deals
Strong technical aptitude with the ability to quickly grasp and articulate complex product features
Demonstrated success in onboarding and ramping up new sales hires
Self-starter mentality with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving startup environment
Data-driven approach to measuring the impact of enablement initiatives
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships across all levels of the organization
Flexibility to adapt to changing priorities and take on additional responsibilities as needed
 Bonus points if you have: 
Experience as a practitioner in audit/advisory, ideally in a corporate internal audit function (CIA, CPA, or CISA a plus)
Working knowledge of internal audit, SOX, and enterprise risk, and/or public sector procurement and compliance frameworks
Experience selling to or working in government (federal, state, local, or education), including RFP and procurement processes
 More about Fieldguide: 
Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:
Fearless - Inspire & break down seemingly impossible walls.
Fast - Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.
Lovable - ​​Deliver happiness & 11 star experiences.
Owners - Execute & run the business with ownership.
Win-win - Create mutual value & earn trust for life.
Inclusive - Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams.
 Some of our benefits include: 
Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership
Unlimited PTO
401k
Wellness benefits, including a bundle of free therapy sessions
Technology & Work from Home reimbursement
Flexible work schedules

This is a US-based remote position. We have a strong preference for candidates based in North Carolina or New York, where our team hubs are.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Customer Relationships 
Own the relationship for your portfolio of accounts, from late-stage sales through onboarding and ongoing partnership.
Join late-stage sales conversations to help set realistic expectations before contract signature.
Build trusted relationships with executive, clinical, operational, and technical stakeholders, and keep building them as people and priorities change.
Be the customer’s advocate inside Keebler Health, making sure their needs, feedback, and concerns reach Product, Engineering, and Clinical teams and get answered.
Understand each customer’s goals, challenges, and measures of success, and tell their story clearly to our internal teams.
Develop account plans, stakeholder maps, and communication rhythms for each account.
Lead regular business reviews, executive check-ins, and planning conversations.
Be a key part of renewals, and help customers get the most from their relationship with us by identifying additional features and opportunities that fit their goals.
Monitor account health and address risks, gaps, and opportunities before the customer has to raise them.
 Managing a Portfolio 
Balance competing priorities across several customers, deciding where your time and our team’s time will have the most impact.
Manage requests, issues, and escalations through to resolution, coordinating with Implementation, Support, Product, Engineering, and Clinical teams.
Set honest expectations with customers about timing and scope, and say no or not yet when you need to.
Keep commitments visible so that important details do not fall through the cracks.
Hold stakeholders, internal and external, accountable while maintaining strong working relationships.
 Working with Implementation 
Partner with the Implementation team through onboarding so the handoff to ongoing account management is smooth and nothing is lost.
Drive adoption across practices and user groups, including bringing on new users and sites over time.
Share structured customer feedback and contribute to repeatable customer success processes and playbooks.
 What Success Looks Like 
We're moving fast as a company, and things will change rapidly, but below is a sense of what success could look like in this role:
First 30 days: learn our platform, customers, and internal teams, and meet the stakeholders for your accounts as well as take ownership of steady state customers.
First 90 days: own your account portfolio, with account plans in place and your first quarterly business reviews completed.
First year: customers who are live and using the platform, clear measures of value, and renewals or expansions that reflect it.
 About You 
 Your Experience 
3-5+ years in customer success, account management, or another customer-facing role, ideally in software.
A track record of owning customer relationships and growing or renewing accounts, with measurable results.
Sales skills: you are comfortable running a commercial conversation, spotting an opening, and asking for the next step.
Credibility with senior customers and the confidence to have difficult conversations.
Strong organization and the ability to juggle competing priorities across several accounts without dropping the ball.
Ability to work with technical and non-technical teams without direct authority.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Comfortable working in an early-stage or rapidly changing environment.
Value-based care or healthcare technology experience is a nice to have, not a requirement. If you’re strong in the rest and curious about the industry, we want to hear from you.
 How You Work 
Takes ownership of outcomes and drives them forward independently.
Combines real empathy for the customer with operational discipline.
Stays calm and clear under pressure, including when a customer is unhappy.
Advocates for customers without losing sight of what is realistic for Keebler Health.
Communicates credibly with everyone from a clinician inside a practice to an executive inside a parent organization.
Motivated by compounding results, where the second year of an account is stronger because of how the first year was run.
Uses LLMs and AI tools to remove friction and build capacity, and improves the team’s systems alongside their own output.
 What We Offer 
Competitive salary, equity options, and benefits package.
A fast-paced, innovative environment.
Professional growth and development opportunities.
A collaborative and supportive team culture.
The chance to shape a foundational role and make a meaningful impact on the healthcare industry.

About Us:
 AI needs a new infrastructure layer. We're building it at Modal.
Every era of computing brought new workloads that previous infrastructure couldn't support: mainframes, databases, and the cloud. Each time, the company that rebuilt the layer underneath defined the decade. AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now.
Our customers include category-defining companies like Ramp , Cognition, DoorDash, and Suno. They rely on Modal for instant GPU access, sub-second container starts, and native storage, so it's simple to serve low-latency inference, fine-tune models, and access production-ready sandboxes at scale.
We've passed $1B in annualized run rate, up 15x from a year ago. In October 2026 we raised a $750M Series D led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation.
Our team includes creators of popular open-source projects (e.g., Seaborn , Luigi ), academic researchers, international olympiad medalists, and experienced engineering and product leaders with decades of experience.
The Role:
We’re seeking a Revenue Operations Manager with a strong track record, a builder’s mindset, and a bias for action to join our in-person team in London.
This is a high-impact, hands-on role. You’ll own the entire revenue operations function, from top-of-funnel lead routing through deal close and commission administration. You’ll work closely with our Head of Finance & People Ops and sales leadership to build the systems, dashboards, and processes that scale our go-to-market motion.
What You’ll Work On:
Own the inbound lead routing process, partnering with Marketing to ensure proper attribution
Run territory management and strategy for geo-based decision-making
Support and strategize on every aspect of revenue operations in your territory
Own capacity forecasting strategy, including inputs, throughputs, and outputs, and serve as the conduit back to Finance in the US for effective capacity forecasting
Provide input and strategy on comp-based decisions and benchmarking
Support leadership on overall regional operations and finance strategy across all functions, including sales, presales, and ecosystem
Evaluate new tools on the market and be responsible for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the sales team
Build and maintain dashboards, leaderboards, and pipeline reporting to give leadership real-time visibility
Monitor deal progression and hold reps accountable for CRM hygiene and accuracy
Support deal reviews at the pricing and negotiation stages, coordinating with outside counsel as needed
Own the closed-won process from signature through handoff to post-sale
Administer commission plans across the sales org, ensuring accurate and timely calculations and serving as the source of truth for comp-related questions
You May Be a Fit If:
You have 3–7 years in Sales Operations or Revenue Operations at a high-growth, usage-based sales organization
You’ve built core GTM infrastructure before: lead routing, CRM architecture, pipeline reporting, commission administration, and deal desk
You have deep proficiency in CRM workflows, lifecycle stages, custom properties, and data hygiene
You’ve owned commissions end-to-end: building the model, calculating payouts, fielding rep disputes, and keeping it reconciled with Finance
You’ve run a deal desk, know what makes a contract clean, and catch errors before they become problems
You’re strong in Excel or Google Sheets: you can build a pipeline coverage model and know which metrics actually matter
You’ve earned trust with a sales team by making their lives easier while holding them accountable to process
You have a builder’s mentality: you identify gaps, propose solutions, and execute without being asked twice
You can zoom out and think strategically while staying close enough to the work to get your hands on the keyboard
You have an AI-forward mindset: you actively use AI in your work and are excited to pioneer its use in go-to-market operations
You have strong communication and collaboration skills and earn trust across Sales, Marketing, and Finance
You’re a player-coach: you’re not above the details, and you’re excited to own the work yourself

At FintechOS, we are looking for a Sales Operations Lead who wants to build, influence, and leave a visible mark. You will shape the processes, data, technology, and commercial rhythms behind our global enterprise sales organisation, creating an environment where the commercial team can focus, execute consistently, and thrive.
This is not a CRM administration role. You will have the mandate to challenge what is not working, simplify how we operate, and turn HubSpot into a genuine performance enabler. Your impact will be visible in seller productivity, pipeline quality, forecast confidence, and our ability to scale.
 Why this role is worth your next move 
• Build, do not simply maintain: shape the sales operating model and HubSpot environment for our next stage of growth.
• Influence at the right level: partner with senior commercial leaders on forecasting, planning, performance, and go-to-market decisions.
• Own outcomes end to end: identify the problem, design the solution, lead adoption, and measure the commercial impact.
• Solve meaningful complexity: enable enterprise sales into banks, insurers, and other highly regulated organisations.
The impact you will make
 Build the sales operating system: Create scalable processes and cadences that help sellers prioritise the right accounts, progress complex opportunities, and execute consistently.
 Make HubSpot work for sellers: Own CRM architecture, pipeline design, workflows, automation, integrations, reporting, data governance, and adoption.
 Increase seller productivity: Remove unnecessary administration, automate repetitive work, and return more time to customer-facing activity.
 Own the revenue execution cadence: Run pipeline inspection, deal reviews, forecast cadence, and the shared sales scoreboard, turning each into clear decisions, actions, and accountability.
 Turn data into decisions: Give sellers, managers, and leaders clear insight into priorities, risks, performance, and growth opportunities.
 Enable complex deals: Improve pricing, approvals, contracting, and cross-functional coordination across long enterprise sales cycles.
 Shape commercial planning: Partner with Sales Leadership and Finance on territories, quotas, capacity, coverage, and performance management.
 Lead meaningful change: Take operational improvements from idea through implementation, enablement, adoption, and measurable impact.
What you will bring
8+ years in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Commercial Operations, ideally within enterprise B2B SaaS.
Advanced HubSpot experience across CRM architecture, pipeline design, automation, reporting, integrations, data governance, and user adoption.
Experience supporting long, high-value sales cycles involving multiple decision-makers, procurement, legal, security, and executive stakeholders.
Hands-on ownership of forecasting, pipeline governance, territory planning, quota setting, or capacity planning.
Strong knowledge of ARR, ACV, bookings, pipeline coverage, win rate, sales velocity, and quota attainment.
Strong analytical and modelling skills using Excel or Google Sheets, plus Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or similar tools.
A track record of simplifying sales processes and improving seller productivity without sacrificing commercial discipline.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and change leadership skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively.
Great to have

We help organisations build workforce readiness through flexible learning, compliance, and talent development solutions designed for complex and highly regulated environments across both the public and private sectors. 
 The Senior Customer Success Manager (Senior CSM) is responsible for building strong, strategic relationships with Totara’s UK Public Sector customers to drive long-term value, customer satisfaction, retention, and growth. Transitioning from a traditional Senior Client Relationship Management approach, this role places a stronger emphasis on proactive customer engagement, business outcomes, adoption, value realisation, partnership, and developing sector-level networks and retention.

Working cross-functionally with Sales, Support, Professional Services, Product, and Partners, the CSM champions the customer experience throughout the lifecycle. 
 Customer Success & Relationship Management 
 Build and maintain trusted, strategic relationships with assigned customers and key stakeholders within the UK Public Sector at senior levels (including mapping customer stakeholders). 
 Develop a deep understanding of each customer’s business objectives, learning strategy, and success measures. 
 Create and maintain Customer Success Plans aligned to customer goals and desired outcomes. 
 Lead regular customer engagement activities including business reviews, success planning sessions, and adoption discussions. 
 Proactively identify risks to customer satisfaction, engagement, retention, or platform adoption and coordinate resolution plans. 
 Act as the primary point of contact for customer success-related matters. 
 Act as a mentor and role model within the Customer Success team, including allocating and supervising team work, inducting and buddying colleagues, and undertaking line management where required. 
 Support members of the CS team with commercial queries, challenging customer scenarios, and on customer calls (where necessary). 
 Adoption & Value Realisation 
 Drive customer adoption and effective use of Totara products and services. 
 Help customers identify opportunities to maximise value from their Totara investment. 
 Monitor customer health indicators and usage trends to identify opportunities for engagement and improvement. 
 Support customers through organisational change, maturity growth, and evolving business needs. 
 Share best practices, industry insights, and strategic recommendations. 
 Retention & Growth 
 Support customer retention and renewal objectives through strong relationship management and demonstrated value. 
 Identify opportunities for account growth, expansion, and additional services in collaboration with wider commercial teams. 
 Contribute to renewal planning and customer advocacy initiatives. 
 Encourage customer participation in case studies, events, reference programmes, and community activities. 
 Maintain CRM Deal and Pipeline information, to support accurate forecasting and commercial record-keeping. 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration 
 Collaborate closely with Sales, Support, Product, Professional Services, and Partner teams to deliver a seamless customer experience. 
 Advocate for customer needs internally and ensure customer feedback informs product and service improvements. 
 Coordinate internal resources to support customer outcomes and issue resolution. 
 Maintain accurate customer records, engagement notes, and success plans within CRM and customer success systems. 
 Support the design and implementation of process improvements to team systems and functions. 
 Work with the Customer Experience and Marketing teams to lead and participate in virtual and in-person customer events (engagement, focus groups, sector-specific, etc). 
 Why Join Totara? 
 Lead a strategic function with strong executive support. 
 Shape the future of security, trust and resilience for a global SaaS platform. 
 Work with talented colleagues across New Zealand, Australia, the UK and the US. 
 Flexible and hybrid ways of working.

 Enhanced Parental Leave 
 Private Healthcare 
 Life Insurance 4x Salary 
 Professional Development Opportunities 
 Annual Wellbeing Allowance

Manager of Customer Success 
 Who we are: 
We provide the world's engineers mission-critical intelligence, safeguarding the technology of today and enabling the breakthroughs of tomorrow. Accuris transforms the world's largest repository of standards and supply chain data into AI-driven insights and connected workflows - enabling engineers to work smarter, stay compliant, and innovate faster. Behind every world-changing innovation - there's Accuris - the most trusted intelligence platform for engineers. https://accuristech.com/ 
 The Team: 
The Customer Success team partners with our customers from onboarding through renewal to make sure they get lasting value from Accuris. You will lead a team of Customer Success Engineers and Customer Success Managers and work closely with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Content Services to champion the customer's voice and drive retention and growth.
 The Impact: 
As our Manager of Customer Success, you will own renewal rate, churn, and customer satisfaction across our customer base, and be accountable for improving all three. You will build the strategy, programs, and processes that spot churn risk early, transform how customers engage with support from intake through resolution, and strengthen relationships from end users to executive stakeholders. As the Voice of the Customer, you will make sure customer feedback directly shapes our product, content, and go-to-market strategies. Success looks like renewal rate and gross and net revenue retention improving year over year, churn at or below forecast, CSAT/NPS measured consistently and trending up, and at-risk accounts engaged months before renewal, not in the final weeks.
 Responsibilities: 
 Retention & Churn Reduction: Own renewal rate and churn, including the monthly forecast and reporting to leadership; build churn prediction models, customer health scoring, and proactive retention playbooks, and partner with Sales on renewals, expansions, and at-risk account recovery.
 Proactive Customer Engagement: Establish a structured engagement approach across the customer lifecycle, including touchpoints, success milestones, and intervention triggers, and design an onboarding experience that connects early adoption to long-term retention.
 Support Intake & Experience: Build the customer support intake process (channels, routing, prioritization, and self-service), set and enforce SLAs, and resolve complex or high-risk customer situations with confidence.
 Voice of the Customer: Turn customer insights into improvements across Product, Marketing, and Content Services, partnering with Product to prioritize the fixes and features that most affect retention.
 Data & Operational Excellence: Define and track churn, renewal rate, gross and net revenue retention, customer health, NPS/CSAT, and support KPIs, and build the dashboards and scalable processes that drive measurable outcomes.
 Team Leadership: Build, lead, and coach a high-performing team of Customer Success Engineers and Customer Success Managers, with clear goals, accountability, and a culture of continuous improvement.
 What We're Looking For: 
7+ years in Customer Success, Customer Support, or Customer Experience leadership roles.
Experience with electronic component, supply chain, or engineering data products.
Proven track record of reducing churn and improving customer retention, including building or scaling support operations and intake processes.
Experience in SaaS or subscription businesses, with familiarity with customer success platforms, CRM systems, support tools, and health scoring or lifecycle frameworks, is a plus.
Strong analytical skills and a data-driven approach to decisions and outcomes.
Strategic thinker with strong execution, process design, and operational discipline across multiple priorities.
Customer-first mindset focused on long-term value.
Strong communication, stakeholder management, and cross-functional influence with Sales, Product, and Marketing.
 The Location: 
Remote - US East Coast preferred
 Compensation/Benefits Information: 
Accuris states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $100,000 to $112,000 . Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual's geographical location as well as experience and qualifications for the role. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan as well as comprehensive benefits. For more information on benefits, please reach out to the recruiter assigned to the role.
 Company Statement: 
Accuris provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

At UKG, the work you do matters. The code you ship, the decisions you make, and the care you show a customer all add up to real impact. We never stop learning. We never stop challenging the norm. We push for better, and we celebrate the wins along the way. Here, you’ll get flexibility that’s real, benefits you can count on, and a team that succeeds together. Because at UKG, your work matters — and so do you.
 About the team 
The Partner Ecosystem and Strategic Engagement organization uses data, reporting, and business insights to support partner performance and strategic growth. The Analytics & Insights function provides reliable reporting, analytical visibility, and decision support for business leaders.
You’ll partner closely with the Senior Business Program Manager and Strategic Engagement leadership. This role owns the analytical products, reporting, and evidence, while the Senior Business Program Manager owns business cadence, resulting actions, and cross-functional accountability.
 About the role 
As an Analytics & Insights professional, you’ll build the trusted analytical foundation for Partner Ecosystem and Strategic Engagement. You’ll develop recurring performance reporting, analyze pipeline and forecast data, identify trends and exceptions, and translate complex information into clear findings that support business decisions.
Your work will help leaders understand performance, investigate risks and opportunities, and make decisions using consistent, well-documented data.

Analyze pipeline, bookings, forecasts, activity, and agreed-upon business metrics.
Identify trends, variances, anomalies, and performance patterns.
Develop segment, partner, account, territory, and comparative analyses.
Build and maintain recurring dashboards, scorecards, and performance views.
Create repeatable weekly, monthly, and executive reporting outputs.
Translate business requirements into clear analytical products and reporting specifications.
Analyze pipeline composition, movement, coverage, and forecast signals.
Surface material variances, risks, and areas requiring further business investigation.
Provide analytical inputs for forecast and performance discussions without owning business commitments.
Conduct whitespace, account-targeting, territory, and coverage analyses.
Identify patterns that may represent growth opportunities, performance gaps, or resource needs.
Support scenario modeling and strategic planning with fact-based analysis.
Monitor data consistency, tagging, and reporting inputs.
Document key performance indicator (KPI) logic, metric definitions, assumptions, and source lineage.
Own reporting quality assurance and identify data-quality conditions that could affect decision-making.
Produce Partner Ecosystem and Strategic Engagement dashboards, pipeline and forecast views, partner creation and co-sell measurement, trend and exception analyses, and executive analytical exhibits.
Provide ad hoc strategic analysis and decision support as needed.
 How success is measured: 
Leaders have reliable, consistent, and timely analytical visibility.
Metric definitions, assumptions, and reporting logic are documented and understood.
Recurring reporting becomes increasingly repeatable and less manually intensive.
Analytics surfaces meaningful trends, exceptions, risks, and opportunities.
Business leaders can trace findings to trusted data and use them to make decisions.
 About you 
You’re an analytical and detail-oriented professional who can turn complex business data into clear, useful insights. You bring strong reporting and dashboard skills, structured problem-solving abilities, and the communication skills needed to explain findings to business and executive audiences.

Post-Sales Enablement Manager 
 Backblaze (Nasdaq: BLZE) | Reports to the Director of Customer Programs | Remote
 Salary range: [$145,000-$165,000]
 How We Got Here 
Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Together with our partners, we're helping customers break free from the restrictive, overpriced legacy solutions that hold them back, and blaze forward with the full power of the open cloud in their hands.
We started by building storage servers from scratch in a Palo Alto apartment to save 90% on hardware. Turns out hard constraints make for pretty good engineering. That discipline forged a platform that performs as well or better than competitors, scales to multi-exabyte workloads, and costs a fraction of what AWS or Google charge. AI infrastructure runs on data. Storage gets hard at scale. We've been breaking, rebuilding, and improving that storage layer for 20 years.
Today, the world's leading AI infrastructure providers, neoclouds, and data-intensive businesses run on Backblaze. Our platform includes:
 B2 Overdrive - high-throughput object storage engineered for AI infrastructure, GPU workloads, and massive-scale data pipelines
 B2 Neo - white-label enterprise cloud storage powering neocloud platforms for AI, HPC, and media
 B2 Cloud Storage - S3-compatible object storage with predictable pricing, free egress, and no lock-in
 Computer Backup - automatic, continuous endpoint backup for Macs and PCs
500,000+ customers. 175 countries. Nasdaq: BLZE. backblaze.com
 The Role 
Reporting to the Director of Customer Programs, we need an operator to own enablement for a post-sales organization that is growing fast: Support, Customer Success, Customer Growth, Adoption and Flagship Account Management. Every new hire, product release and system change has to become something our teams can do on day one. You will own how that happens, end to end: the strategy, training, standards and cadence that keep every post-sales role ramped and current. You are the first dedicated owner of this work, and you will define it while the organization roughly doubles its individual contributors in 2027.
This is a senior individual contributor role with a trusted-advisor relationship to the VP and post-sales leaders. You will work alongside the CX Enablement Specialist, who also reports to the Director and knows how Backblaze really works: the backend, customer provisioning, the core systems and Salesforce. The Specialist brings deep knowledge of how things work here, and you bring structure and learning design. Together you turn that knowledge into learning paths and training that every new hire can follow, and you shape how the two of you share the work.
You have built and run post-sales teams, you know how to turn chaos into a working system, and you bring a point of view on how a post-sales organization should be enabled at scale.
 What You Will Own 
 Build 
The post-sales enablement strategy and multi-quarter roadmap, tied to the 2027 plan and to the metrics each team is accountable for. You present it to the VP and post-sales leaders and adjust it as the business changes.
A clear read on where teams struggle, using scorecard data and conversations with leaders, and the judgment to decide which gaps to close first.
The enablement operating model: how enablement is requested, built, approved, updated and retired, the quality standard for all content, and who owns what.
Role-based learning paths, skill levels and a formal certification and badging framework, designed with the post-sales leaders, so each role has a clear way to progress and to prove readiness.
Formal onboarding for Customer Success managers and Support, where onboarding today is largely informal, then extended to Growth, Adoption and Flagship. You run it through the 2027 hiring wave so new hires reach productivity quickly and consistently.
The release-to-enablement process with Product: product releases and roadmap changes turned into training, talking points and resources for each role, ready before customers ask.

 Account Team Partnership: Work as one account team with your AE, TAM and Solutions Architect. Bring in Product, Support and Engineering when the account needs them, so the customer experiences one cohesive Buildkite. 
 Cadence Design: Determine when and how to engage each account based on the value it returns to the customer — right-sizing engagement so every interaction earns its place on the customer’s calendar.
 Operating Model Contribution: Help shape the playbooks, processes, and operating model of a maturing CS function — and mentor new team members as the team grows. 
 Executive Influence and Customer Partnership 
 Executive Engagement: Cultivate and maintain trusted relationships with customer C-suite, VP, Director, and program-owner stakeholders — including the executive sponsor accountable for the Buildkite investment.
 Business Translation: Translate technical adoption and platform health into the business outcomes that matter to executive sponsors, and into the language they use with their own leadership.
 Executive Business Reviews: Lead the EBR cadence with the AE and TAM — bringing the value narrative, customer readiness, and forward-looking strategy that keeps the partnership on track.
 Customer Advocacy: Amplify the voice of the customer inside Buildkite, ensuring Product, Engineering, and Support stay focused on what matters most to the accounts you own.
 Risk, Renewal, and Expansion Readiness 
 Account Health: Maintain a live view of technical, commercial, support, and relationship signals across your portfolio — surface risk early, mobilize the right Buildkite resources, and prevent escalation through proactive partnership.
 Renewal Strategy: Partner with the Account Executive on renewal strategy by driving the value narrative, customer readiness, and account health that underpin every commercial conversation.
 Expansion Sourcing: Identify and source expansion opportunities through the Customer-Sourced Qualified Lead (CSQL) process — turning customer outcomes into growth.
 Onboarding: Partner with the Technical Account Manager on the first 90 days, and sustain the joint CSM/TAM cadence that drive
[...]
established one 
 Benefits 
 Work from anywhere in the world for up to 6 weeks a year, on top of a fully remote setup — great work doesn’t have to happen from one desk.
 20 days paid annual leave plus 10 days sick & carer's leave — actively encouraged, we want you to be at your best and time off is a part of that.
 16 weeks paid parental leave for primary carers (6 for secondary) — becoming a parent is life changing and we’re committed to supporting you and your family through it.
 A remote-work allowance for home-office kit, co-working, or working elsewhere — we want you to have everything you need to be set up for success in your role.
 Confidential EAP & mental health support — sometimes life gets hard. You should be able to access the resources and support you need.
 Support for learning and growth — with time and budget for conferences, courses, and coaching so you have the opportunity to grow, improve your craft, and build mastery.
 Retirement and health coverage (based on your region) — build towards your future, your way.

About Extend: 
Extend is revolutionizing the post-purchase experience for retailers and their customers by providing merchants with AI-driven solutions that enhance customer satisfaction and drive revenue growth. Our comprehensive platform offers automated customer service handling, seamless returns/exchange management, end-to-end automated fulfillment, and product protection and shipping protection alongside Extend's best-in-class fraud detection. By integrating leading-edge technology with exceptional customer service, Extend empowers businesses to build trust and loyalty among consumers while reducing costs and increasing profits.
Today, Extend works with more than 1,000 leading merchant partners across industries, including fashion/apparel, cosmetics, furniture, jewelry, consumer electronics, auto parts, sports and fitness, and much more. Extend is backed by some of the most prominent technology investors in the industry, and our headquarters is in downtown San Francisco.
 About The Role 
Our Growth & Sales teams hear something new from merchants every day: a coverage gap that cost us a deal, a feature our partners keep asking for, a trend in the data nobody has acted on yet. The way we win is by connecting those signals and turning them into something that will grow revenue for Extend and our merchant partners.
We are looking for a GTM Strategy & Program Manager to own that feedback loop for a portfolio of retail verticals. You will listen to what our merchant partners want and need, decide what is worth building, drive the right teams to build it in a scalable way, and make sure your Pod knows exactly how to sell it. Your success shows up in new deals won, existing partnerships grown, and stronger margins on both.
This is a role for someone who presents ideas without hesitation, can hold a room with leaders, and never settles for not knowing the answer.
 What You’ll Do 
 Own the feedback loop. Run a regular cadence with Sales, Growth and Analytics to pull together merchant feedback, win/loss reasons and performance data, and turn it into a clear, prioritized view of what we need to build to win more.
 Grow the top and bottom line. Find the opportunities that win new merchants and expand existing partnerships, and build the business case for each one in terms of revenue and margin impact.
 Turn merchant needs into scalable solutions. Listen to what our partners are asking for and shape it into products, features and program offerings that work across your verticals, not one-off custom builds.
 Run the project plan. Set scope, milestones and owners for every initiative, hold teams accountable to deadlines, and raise risks early when something starts to slip.
 Know exactly what is being built. Understand every feature well enough to explain how it works, who it is for and where its limits are, from requirements through launch.
 Enable your Pod. Equip your vertical Pod with the playbooks, talk tracks and training they need to sell and use each new feature, and track adoption after launch.
 Present with conviction. Pitch new ideas to cross-functional partners, executives and leadership, back your recommendations with data, and drive the decision.
 Go find the answer. When a question comes up that nobody can answer, dig into the data, the contracts or the market yourself and come back with the answer and a recommendation.
 Required Qualifications 
 Relevant experience. 5+ years in GTM Strategy, BizOps, or a similar cross-functional role at a fast-paced tech company.
 Ownership from idea to launch. You have taken an initiative from a customer or partner need through build, launch and enablement, and can point to the commercial results.
 Project management discipline. You run several initiatives in parallel, set realistic plans and keep cross-functional teams on deadline without being chased.
 Executive presence. You put ideas in front of people early and often, present to executives with conviction, and hold your ground when you have the data to back it up.
 A numbers-first mindset. Advanced Excel and strong analytical skills. You size opportunities, build models and root your recommendations in data.
 Relentless curiosity. You do not accept "we don't know" as an answer. You go dig it up and report back.
 An AI-native way of working. You already use AI tools like Claude to research, analyze and move faster, and you pick up new tools quickly.
 Nice To Have 
SQL or BI tool experience
Experience in retail, finance, or consulting
Exposure to underwriting concepts like frequency, severity and loss ratio
 Expected Pay Range: $125,000 - $135,000 per year salaried
 *The target base salary range for this position is listed above. Individual salaries are determined based on a number of factors including, but not limited to, job-related knowledge, skills and experience. 
 Extend does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. 
 Life at Extend: 
 Working with a great team from diverse backgrounds in a collaborative and supportive environment. 
 Competitive salary based on experience, with full medical and dental & vision benefits. 
 Stock in an early-stage startup growing quickly. 
 Generous, flexible paid time off policy. 
 401(k) with Financial Guidance from Morgan Stanley.

About Us
Mighty Networks helps people and brands build communities, online courses, memberships, challenges, and events. Through its advanced technology, called people magic, Mighty helps the members of those networks build relationships with each other by surfacing the most relevant and interesting connections. 
Because of this novel approach and member-centered experience, Mighty has produced the most $1M communities and helped its Hosts earn over $500M.
The Role
At Mighty Networks, we believe communities are the next generation of digital business. As a Customer Success Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring our Mighty Pro Hosts achieve outstanding success. You will act as their primary partner, helping them unlock their community’s potential and exceed their goals through proactive engagement, strategic guidance, and ongoing relationship management. The ideal candidate is results-driven, strategic, and committed to ensuring our Hosts see measurable success.

Serve as the primary relationship owner from the moment a Pro Host signs with Mighty through renewal and beyond, ensuring a seamless and positive experience throughout the customer lifecycle.
Develop and deliver custom quotes for additional services, aligning with Hosts' evolving needs and business objectives.
Partner with Mighty Pro Hosts to increase adoption of key product features that will lead to great engagement and retention within their community.
Map out a compelling success plan for each Mighty Pro Host, aiming to exceed their goals and deliver results beyond their initial expectations.
Proactively anticipate and plan for key moments and milestones in the annual life of a Mighty Pro Host, ensuring timely interventions and support.
Identify and mitigate risks to our long-term relationships with Mighty Pro Hosts, collaborating with cross-functional teams to address challenges promptly.
Creatively generate value by ensuring clear goals, key milestones, frequent check-ins, and Host and member satisfaction—capturing and sharing best practices from across our entire Customer Success function.
Communicate consistently and methodically with Mighty Pro Hosts and internal teams, including leadership, marketing, product, and customer advocacy, to ensure continuous improvement and scalability of Host results.
Own the renewal process from start to finish, proactively engaging Hosts well in advance of their renewal date, addressing concerns, demonstrating ongoing value, and securing long-term commitments.
What We're Looking For
Proven experience in Customer Success, with a track record of delivering exceptional results for clients.
Strong organizational and relationship-building skills, with the ability to manage complex client relationships and navigate challenging conversations effectively.
Experience managing high-value accounts, demonstrating the ability to help successful brands, entrepreneurs, and creators build incredible businesses through the power of community.
A proactive and dynamic approach, thriving in a fast-paced, rapidly growing environment, and constantly seeking ways to enhance impact and value creation.
Curiosity and active listening skills, with a passion for community-powered businesses and a desire to be part of building a new and critical team at a pioneering startup.
Confidence in executive communication, both with high-profile Hosts and internal leaders, ensuring clear and effective dialogue.
A desire to drive innovation, helping creators, entrepreneurs, and brands make the biggest impact in 2027 and beyond.
Ability to implement feedback loops to capture customer insights and inform product development and service enhancements.
An entrepreneurial mindset — you understand what it takes to build something from nothing, which gives you a natural empathy for the creators, entrepreneurs, and brands you'll serve.
A genuine curiosity about AI-driven solutions, consistently exploring how emerging tools can enhance customer outcomes, streamline your own workflows, and unlock new ways for community-powered businesses to grow and thrive.
What We Offer
A dynamic, remote-first work culture that values creativity, autonomy, and bold thinking.
Comprehensive benefits, including health, vision, dental, and paid time off.
Clear opportunities for professional growth, including leadership pathways and skill development support.
The chance to shape the future of how communities, creators, and brands thrive online—with the team that’s building what’s next.
Join us in shaping the future of community-driven digital businesses with Mighty Pro!
 Compensation: The base salary for this role ranges from $70,000–$125,000, with exact compensation based on location, experience, and cost of living.

Founded in 2004, NetBrain is the leader in no-code network automation. Its ground-breaking Next-Gen platform provides IT operations teams with the ability to scale their hybrid multi-cloud connected networks by automating the processes associated with Diagnostic Troubleshooting, Outage Prevention and Protected Change Management. Today, over 2,500 of the world’s largest enterprises and managed services providers leverage NetBrain’s platform. 
 What We Need 
 NetBrain is looking for a Customer Success Manager (CSM) located in the Southeastern United States to own the full lifecycle of our customer relationships — from onboarding through adoption, expansion, and renewal. 
 At NetBrain, CSMs are strategic partners to our customers — operators of complex enterprise networks spanning thousands of devices. You'll help them unlock the full value of NetBrain's Agentic NetOps platform: no-code automation, real-time digital twin visibility, and AI-assisted network diagnosis. You'll do this by building deep relationships, driving measurable outcomes, and ensuring every customer renews and grows. 
 What You'll Do 
 This is a full-ownership role. You are the primary post-sale contact for a portfolio of enterprise accounts. 
 You own every renewal in your portfolio — from 12-month strategic planning through executed contract signature. GRR ≥ 90% and NRR ≥ 105% are your metrics. You run the process; Sales supports you. 
 Relationship Management 
 Build and own multi-threaded stakeholder maps across IT Operations, Network Engineering, and executive leadership. 
 Run monthly check-ins, semi-annual QBRs, and annual Executive Business Reviews (EBRs) for strategic accounts. 
 Serve as the primary escalation point for your customers and the voice of the customer internally. 
 Adoption & Value Realization 
 Define customer-specific success metrics at contract start and track them throughout the lifecycle. 
 Monitor product health via adoption dashboards; address low-utilization signals proactively. 
 Deliver data-driven QBR materials that demonstrate ROI against stated business outcomes. 
 Renewal Ownership (Full Cycle) 
 Open and manage renewal opportunities in Salesforce 12 months before contract end. 
 Lead the end-to-end renewal timeline: health assessment (9mo), executive alignment (6mo), proposal (4mo), negotiation and legal coordination (2mo), close (30 days out). 
 Maintain renewal forecast accuracy within ±5% of final ARR vs. 60-day projection. 
 Escalate at-risk accounts (churn probability > 50%) to VP CS within 24 hours with a joint recovery plan. 
 Expansion & Growth 
 Identify and qualify upsell opportunities across NetBrain modules, user seats, and new use cases. 
 Maintain an expansion pipeline at ≥ 3× quarterly quota coverage in Salesforce. 
 Partner with the Account Executive on joint proposals and POC planning for new module evaluations. 
 Internal Advocacy 
 Submit customer feature requests through Product feedback channels and relay roadmap updates during QBRs. 
 Nominate satisfied customers for case studies, references, and advisory board participation. 
 Log all customer activity in Salesforce within 24 hours; maintain renewal health scorecard at each milestone. 
 What You Bring 
 8+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a related post-sale role in B2B enterprise software. 
 Demonstrated ownership of renewal cycles — including negotiation, legal coordination, and ARR accountability. 
 Experience managing a portfolio of complex enterprise accounts. 
 Strong executive presence — comfortable presenting QBRs and EBRs to VP/C-level stakeholders. 
 Proficiency with Salesforce CRM for pipeline management, activity logging, and forecasting. 
 Ability to interpret product usage and adoption data and translate it into customer-facing narratives. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills; strong follow-through and organizational habits. 
 Preferred 
 Experience in network management, IT operations, or infrastructure software (network automation, observability, or adjacent categories). 
 Familiarity with Gainsight or a comparable CS platform. 
 Experience coordinating with Legal and Finance on contract negoti
[...]
ds and fingers for using a computer. 
 Stationary Tasks: Sitting for extended periods, remaining in a stationary position. 
 What We Offer 
 Our comprehensive compensation package is vital in how we recognize our people for the impact they make on us reaching our goals as a company. 
 For this role, the estimated OTE is $150,000 -$200,000. The actual salary may vary based on a range of factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process.

Pindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions. Powered by the Pindrop Intelligence Network, our unified trust platform helps enterprises answer three critical questions:
 Is this identity synthetic? Detect AI-generated and manipulated voice and video.
 Is this identity risky? Identify fraud, suspicious behavior, and other risk signals.
 Is this identity known? Authenticate identities using voice, device, behavioral, and other signals.
Pindrop brings this intelligence together across purpose-built trust engines to help organizations make informed decisions in real time — protecting customers, workforce interactions, and emerging AI-driven interactions.

Which is why we’ve built the world's first, and only, open and hardware-independent service delivery platform for smart homes, small businesses, enterprises, and beyond. Our SaaS platform uses WiFi, advanced AI, and machine learning to create the future of connected spaces—and human experiences—at massive scale. 
 We now deliver services to over 60 million locations globally and have managed over 3 billion devices on our platform. We’re expanding rapidly, pioneering a new category, and we achieved our Series F funding in just four years. Our customers include many of the world's largest Internet Service Providers (ISPs) who look to Plume to help them evolve their smart home offerings while gleaning insights from their own data. 
 With a bias for action and a love for being trailblazers, the team at Plume embodies a combination of relentless curiosity and imaginative innovation. We challenge ourselves to think in ways that other companies don't, work to do what should be done (rather than what can), and if we can’t do it exceptionally well, we don’t do it. It’s how we've assembled a team of world-class builders, thinkers, and doers. And it’s how we’re reinventing what’s possible every day. 
 The Opportunity 
 Plume is looking for a Technical Program Manager to join our Customer Experience organization, reporting directly to the VP of Customer Experience. This role sits at the intersection of technical delivery, program management, and customer success, acting as the connective tissue between our Product and engineering teams, and the Customer Success organization that supports our operator partners. You'll be the technical prime who ensures our solutions genuinely fit customer needs, the program lead who keeps cross-functional delivery on track, and the steady hand who guides the Customer Success team through change as new capabilities roll out.

 Serve as the technical intermediary between end customers and the Network Operations Center (NOC), triaging issues surfaced by customers, routing them to the right team, and ensuring timely resolution with clear communication back to all stakeholders. 
 Support core PMO functions for the Customer Experience organization: maintaining program trackers, status reporting, and risk/issue logs, and running the cadences that keep leadership informed. 
 Partner closely with the VP of Customer Experience to prioritize initiatives, flag risks early, and represent the voice of the customer in technical and delivery conversations. 
 Build strong working relationships across Customer Success, NOC, Engineering, and Product, so technical issues and program updates move quickly and don't get lost between teams.

 Comfortable translating between technical and non-technical audiences, from engineering and the NOC to Customer Success and executive leadership. 
 A natural bridge-builder who can guide a team through change and bring people along during transitions, not just announce them. 
 Calm and methodical under pressure when triaging live, customer-impacting technical issues.

Senior Product Marketing Manager, Sales Enablement (AI & Research): 
 Team: Marketing 
 Prolific 
 Prolific isn’t just enabling AI innovation – we’re redefining it. While foundational AI technologies are becoming commoditized, Prolific’s human data infrastructure provides the high-quality, diverse data required to train the next generation of AI models. Through our platform, we empower researchers and companies to access a global, ethically curated participant base, ensuring cutting-edge AI research and training grounded in inclusivity and precision. 
 The role 
T his is a brand new role, and you’ll be the first person to do it at Prolific. 
 Right now, the insight that could help us win more deals is scattered. We have valuable learnings about why we win, why we lose, and why deals stall, but they aren’t turned into the pitch, proof and materials that sellers use every day. You’ll fix that. You’ll become the person who knows our market position inside out and turns it into tools that help sellers win. 
 This is a revenue role. It sits at the point where product marketing meets sales enablement, across both our AI and research businesses. You’ll dig into win-loss, competitive intelligence and customer proof, then turn it into pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, case studies and training that reps use on their next call. You’ll also help new AEs and SDRs get up to speed faster. 
 You’ll be measured on win rate, sales cycle length, rep ramp time and how well equipped our sellers are in front of a buyer. 
 Our AI PMM leads strategic lab and enterprise AI pursuits, and our vertical PMMs tailor messaging for specific audiences. You own the foundation they all build on: the shared, trusted system of resources every other deal runs on. 
 What you’ll bring to the role 
 6+ years in an enablement-facing role (product marketing, sales enablement or competitive intelligence) at a B2B company 
 Experience enabling sellers across more than one product or product line, at a startup, scale-up or enterprise 
 Experience doing the full job, not just the final slides: you’ve gathered the data and insight yourself, then turned it into materials sellers use 
 Enablement you’ve built that measurably moved win rate, ramp time or deal velocity. You can show who used it and what changed 
 Hands-on experience running buyer interviews. You ask about past behaviour, not hypothetical opinions, and you can get a lost buyer to tell you the real reason 
 Comfort with data: you can pull from a CRM and call-intelligence tools, build an analysis or business case, and defend your conclusions 
 Clear writing for busy readers: short, specific and easy to act on 
 Credibility with sellers and senior leaders, and the ability to get sales, product and customer success to act without managing any of them. You’ll spend a lot of time with sales 
 What you’ll be doing in the role 
 Build and own sales enablement across AI and research: onboarding, ongoing training and launch readiness (with the AI PMM), plus a single source of truth that reps actually use 
 Audit what exists today, decide what stays and what goes, and set up a way to keep it current 
 Build and maintain the core sales toolkit: pitch narrative, decks, one-pagers, discovery guides, battlecards, objection handling, white papers and business-case tools 
 Design and run our win-loss programme: buyer interviews after closed-won, closed-lost and no-decision outcomes, combined with CRM and call data and a regular readout to leadership. You’ll also run one outreach calendar for every AI buyer interview, including the AI PMM’s, so no buyer is asked twice 
 Own competitive intelligence against data labelling vendors, research panel providers and in-house alternatives, including a live view of competitor pricing and positioning that feeds the AI PMM’s category point of view 
 Turn findings into specific changes, such as a new talk track, a revised discovery question or a pricing recommendation, then check whether the change moved the number 
 Own customer proof: case studies with AI and research customers, a sourced library of proof points, the reference programme for live deals, and advocacy through quo
[...]
AI segment win rates the AI PMM is measured on. Work with RevOps to clean up CRM fields for loss reasons and competitor. 
 Why Prolific is a great place to work 
 We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioral data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems. 
 We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviors into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breath and the best of humanity. 
 Working for us will place you at the forefront of AI innovation, providing access to our unique human data platform and opportunities for groundbreaking research. Join us to enjoy a competitive salary, benefits, and remote working within our impactful, mission-driven culture.
For pay transparency, the base salary range for this full-time role in San Francisco or New York is $170,000-$200,000 per annum and negotiable for other states.

Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Senior Sales Operations Manager, you will support the EMEA South Go-To-Market team as a trusted advisor to sales leaders, enabling consistent, predictable, and repeatable hyper-growth through sales discipline, streamlined processes, and a strong operating cadence. You will partner with the EMEA South Leadership Team on GTM design, business analysis, and metrics while managing the day-to-day rhythm of the business, with field productivity as your north star. This role is based in Amsterdam, Prague, or Milan, and is ideal for someone who wants to be an active voice driving change rather than a passive spectator.
What Will You Do?
Primary responsibilities include:
Serve as the EMEA South Operations Lead and trusted advisor to key sales leaders, actively participating in the EMEA forecasting process, advising on changing pipeline dynamics, and challenging forecasts to ensure accuracy, predictability, and transparency.

Drive the annual sales planning process, including Area, Regional, and District goal assignments, territory management updates, and sales compensation plan changes.
Identify gaps in the infrastructure needed to support Sales and develop solutions, with a strong focus on AI, that align to the team’s overall vision, while educating and training teams on key sales processes.
Act as an active voice that drives change with Area leadership, and align with the Global Revenue Operations team to represent the needs of the field.
What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?
Ideal candidates will have:
7 to 10 years of experience in Sales, Revenue, or Field Operations supporting sales teams, with a strong emphasis on enabling teams to be hyper-productive, ideally within organizations selling subscription security software.
Experience designing and scaling processes that support a hyper-growth business model, including documenting key processes in a publicly traded environment.
Proven analytical ability to turn disparate datasets into insightful analytics, including developing messaging, data visualizations, and executive-level presentations.
Solid experience with a key tech stack including Salesforce, Clari, Tableau, MS Office, G-Suite, and AI tools.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to influence sales teams, build collaborative relationships across functions, and translate the complex needs of the field. A Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Management, Technology, or Economics is required, and an MBA is a plus.

The Mid-Market Customer Success team is responsible for driving success, net revenue retention, and expansion within our Mid-Market portfolio. This involves proactively engaging existing merchants, mitigating churn risks, and onboarding new clients. Our team members are experts in the fraud, e-commerce, and payments landscape, collaborating closely with Sales, Implementation, and Risk teams to ensure an exceptional customer experience. We are a results-oriented group focused on delivering significant value and achieving our collective and individual targets.

You will make significant individual contributions to segment goals, including upsell bookings, net profit retention, and year 1 revenue.
You will partner with Sales, Implementation, and Risk teams dedicated to the Mid-Market, along with others, to ensure an exceptional customer experience and achieve your individual targets. You will report to the Director, Customer Success.
We seek enthusiastic individuals eager to master our platform and become experts in the fraud, e-commerce, and payments landscape where we deliver significant value. The ideal candidate is a results-oriented problem solver who is comfortable engaging with a high volume of clients daily.

Oversee the customer lifecycle to proactively drive adoption and ensure ongoing client satisfaction and retention of a portfolio of 30+ assigned clients, using robust, repeatable processes

Identify and successfully close renewals and expansion opportunities within your book of business, analyzing complex situations to provide sophisticated renewal options
Identify and drive new channels for upsell and innovative outreach, particularly approaches that scale across a large portfolio
Have full ownership of commercial activities such as opportunity management and contract workflows, following and improving established processes for a high-volume client base
Proactively identify and address performance trends across your merchant portfolio, such as approval rate and loss rate, through standardized reporting and process adherence
Understand customers’ pain points, initiatives and business goals, and identify how Signifyd can partner to achieve them, translating these insights into actionable, repeatable processes
Ensure swift resolution of account issues by using resources from cross-functional teams and navigating established escalation processes
Provide executive oversight and client communication, ensuring consistent and efficient messaging across a large portfolio
Champion continuous improvement and model disciplined process execution for other te
